body.text:
Cāmuṇḍa (Kāyastha [= Kāyasthacāmuṇḍa], or Caṇḍa; around 1490 CE):
Rasasaṃketakalikā [= Rasasaṅketakalikā]
body.translated_text:
<s>Cāmuṇḍa</s> (<s>Kāyastha</s> [= <s>Kāyasthacāmuṇḍa</s>], or <s>Caṇḍa</s>; around 1490 CE):
<s>Rasasaṃketakalikā</s> [= <s>Rasasaṅketakalikā</s>]

children.translated_text: RSK, 1
Having bowed to <s>Śiva</s>, the lord of <s>rasa</s> (mercury), <s>Cāmuṇḍa</s>, born of the <s>Kāyastha</s> lineage,
composes the <s>Rasasaṃketakalikā</s>, which grants the fulfillment of desires. // Rsk_1.1 //
Mercury: Mythological Origin
For the purpose of slaying <s>Tāraka</s>, <s>Skanda</s>'s [enemy], while [<s>Śambhu</s>] was held by the gods on <s>Kailāsa</s>,

children.text: rate śambhoścyutaṃ reto gṛhītamagninā mukhe // Rsk_1.2 //
children.translated_text: during lovemaking, the semen that fell from <s>Śambhu</s> was received by <s>Agni</s> (fire) in his mouth. // Rsk_1.2 //

children.text: kṣiptaṃ tena caturdikṣu kṣārābdhau tatpṛthak pṛthak /
children.translated_text: He cast it in the four directions, into the alkaline ocean, separately in each;
that which was placed in the three directions beginning with the north does not produce results, due to the curse of <s>Gaurī</s>. // Rsk_1.3 //

body.translated_text: That which was released in the western direction became <s>sūta</s> (mercury), accomplishing all purposes.

children.translated_text: White, reddish, yellowish, and black are the <s>pārada</s> (mercury) types [corresponding to] <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and the other [castes]. // Rsk_1.4 //

body.translated_text: Mercury: Subtypes by Color and Caste

body.text: dehe lohe gade piṣṭyāṃ yojyā vā svasvajātiṣu /
body.translated_text: They should be employed in the body, in metals, in diseases, and in <s>piṣṭī</s> (powder preparations), or each in its own respective class.

children.text: teṣu naisargikā doṣāḥ pañca saptātha kañcukāḥ // Rsk_1.5 //
children.translated_text: Among these, the natural defects are five, then seven <s>kañcukas</s> (sheaths/coverings). // Rsk_1.5 //

body.translated_text: Defects of Mercury

children.text: malādyāḥ pañca doṣāḥ syur bhūjādyāḥ sapta kañcukāḥ /
children.translated_text: The five defects are <s>mala</s> (impurity) and the rest; the seven <s>kañcukas</s> (sheaths) are <s>bhūja</s> (earth-born) and the rest.

children.text: kuṣṭhādīn hi prakurvanti rasasthā dvādaśaiva te // Rsk_1.6 //
children.translated_text: These twelve, present in <s>rasa</s> (mercury), indeed produce <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases) and other [ailments]. // Rsk_1.6 //
The Eighteen Saṃskāras (Purificatory Processes)
Therefore, eighteen <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory processes) have been prescribed by the learned for the removal of defects.

children.text: kartuṃ te duṣkarā yasmāt procyante sukarā rase // Rsk_1.7 //
children.translated_text: Since those are difficult to perform, easy [methods] for <s>rasa</s> (mercury) are [now] described. // Rsk_1.7 //
Mercury: Correct Weight
Starting from one <s>pala</s> up to fifty <s>palas</s> is the [proper quantity of] <s>pārada</s> (mercury);

children.text: tata ūno'dhiko vāpi na saṃskāryo raso budhaiḥ // Rsk_1.8 //
children.translated_text: less or more than that, <s>rasa</s> (mercury) should not be processed by the wise. // Rsk_1.8 //
Saṃskāra: Mardana (Grinding)

children.text: vastre caturguṇe pūtaḥ sūtaḥ sthāpyaḥ śubhe'hani /
children.translated_text: Having purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) through cloth folded fourfold, it should be placed [for processing] on an auspicious day.

children.text: lohārkāśmajakhalve tu tapte caiva vimardayet // Rsk_1.9 //
children.translated_text: One should grind it in a heated mortar made of iron, crystal, or stone. // Rsk_1.9 //
With <s>niśā</s> (turmeric), <s>iṣṭakā</s> (brick powder), <s>surīdhūma</s> (smoke-soot), <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents), sour substances, and salts, each separately,
ground with equal parts of <s>kāla</s> (black pepper), <s>sūta</s> (mercury) becomes purified in a single day. // Rsk_1.10 //

body.text:
<saṃskāra:: svedana>
tataḥ kṣārāmlamūtrādyaiḥ svedyo vastrāvṛto dinam /
body.translated_text:
Saṃskāra: Svedana (Steaming)
Then it should be steamed for a day, wrapped in cloth, with alkaline solutions, acidic substances, urine, and the like.

children.translated_text: Then one should perform <s>mūrchana</s> (swooning/solidification) seven times with <s>kanyā</s> (aloe), <s>agni</s> (Plumbago zeylanica), <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), and <s>varā</s> (Terminalia chebula) juices. // Rsk_1.11 //

body.translated_text: Saṃskāra: Mūrchana (Swooning/Solidifying)

Saṃskāra: Pātana (Distillation)
The purified [mercury], combined with one-quarter part of <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), should be distilled by upward distillation three times.

children.text: hiṅgulād uddhṛtaḥ sūto bhavedvā doṣavarjitaḥ // Rsk_1.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) extracted from <s>hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar) would be free from defects. // Rsk_1.12 //

body.translated_text: Mercury Extracted from Cinnabar: Natural Purity

children.translated_text: Importance of Jāraṇa (Digestion)
Abandoning the teachings of the <s>guru</s>, the fool who prepares <s>rasa</s> (mercury) without <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) that has been digested [into it],

children.text: rasaṃ nirmāti durmedhāḥ śapettaṃ ca raseśvaraḥ // Rsk_1.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Raseśvara</s> (the Lord of Mercury, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>) would curse him. // Rsk_1.13 //
Saṃskāra: Jāraṇa (Digestion of Sulfur into Mercury)

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ rasaikāṃśaṃ stokaṃ stokaṃ tu khalvagam /
children.translated_text: One should add <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) in equal parts to the <s>rasa</s> (mercury), little by little, into the mortar;

children.text: kuṭṭanāt kuṭṭanāt piṣṭaṃ bhavedvā tāmrapātragam // Rsk_1.14 //
children.translated_text: by repeated pounding it becomes a paste, or [it may be done] in a copper vessel. // Rsk_1.14 //

children.text: tattulyaṃ gandhakaṃ dattvā ruddhvā taṃ lohasampuṭe /
children.translated_text: Having added an equal quantity of <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) and sealed it in a metal <s>sampuṭa</s> (covered crucible),

children.text: puṭed bhūdharayantre ca yāvajjīryati gandhakam // Rsk_1.15 //
children.translated_text: one should heat it in a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed crucible furnace) with the <s>bhūdhara-yantra</s> (earth-holding apparatus) until the <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) is digested. // Rsk_1.15 //
In this manner, <s>gandhacūrṇa</s> (sulfur powder) should be added again and again, up to six times the quantity.

children.text: ṣaḍguṇe gandhake jīrṇe raso nikhilarogahā // Rsk_1.16 //
children.translated_text: When sixfold <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) has been digested, the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) destroys all diseases. // Rsk_1.16 //
Bandha (Solidification): Subtypes

children.text: pāṭaḥ khoṭo jalaukā ca bhasmākhyaśca caturthakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Pāṭa</s> (flaky), <s>khoṭa</s> (lumpy), <s>jalaukā</s> (leech-like), and the fourth called <s>bhasma</s> (ash) —
<s>bandha</s> (solidification) of <s>sūta</s> (mercury) is known to be of four types by the best of physicians. // Rsk_1.17 //
<s>Pāṭa</s> is <s>parpaṭikā-bandha</s> (flaky solidification); <s>piṣṭi-bandha</s> (paste solidification) is <s>khoṭaka</s> (lumpy);

children.text: jalaukā pakvabandhaḥ syādbhasma bhasmanibho bhavet // Rsk_1.18 //
children.translated_text: <s>Jalaukā</s> is <s>pakva-bandha</s> (mature solidification); <s>bhasma</s> (ash) becomes ash-like in appearance. // Rsk_1.18 //

body.text:
<mercury:: bhasman:: subtypes>
sūtabhasma dvidhā jñeyamūrdhvagaṃ talabhasma ca /
body.translated_text:
Mercury Bhasma: Subtypes
<s>Sūtabhasma</s> (mercurial ash) should be known as twofold: <s>ūrdhvaga</s> (upper/sublimated) and <s>talabhasma</s> (bottom ash).

children.translated_text: Hear now the apparatus for making <s>ūrdhvabhasma</s> (sublimated ash) — the <s>sthālikā-sampuṭa</s> (pair of earthen pots). // Rsk_1.19 //

body.translated_text: Production of Ūrdhvabhasman (Sublimated Ash)

children.translated_text: Two pots should be made, sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-breadths) on all sides in the middle.
Filling the downward-facing pot with slightly moistened salt, // Rsk_1.20 //
one should smear the joint with cloth and clay, having joined it with the other [pot],
and placing it on a three-doored furnace, cook it with strong fire for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours). // Rsk_1.21 //
After it has cooled on its own, one should remove it and discard the salt.
Making the salt-formed upper layer, <s>Raseśvara</s> (mercury) should be placed in the other [pot]. // Rsk_1.22 //
Having joined [the pots] in a <s>sampuṭa</s> (sealed pair) as before, then place them on the furnace.

children.text: dṛḍhaṃ kṛtvālavālaṃ tu jalaṃ tatra vinikṣipet // Rsk_1.23 //
children.translated_text: Making a firm basin around it, one should pour water into it. // Rsk_1.23 //
Discarding the hot [water] again and again, one should add cold [water] repeatedly.

children.text: tridvāre kāṣṭhamekaikaṃ dīrghaṃ hastamitaṃ kṣipet // Rsk_1.24 //
children.translated_text: In each of the three doors [of the furnace], one should insert one long piece of wood measuring one <s>hasta</s> (cubit). // Rsk_1.24 //
The wise one should first ignite a bundle the size of a fist in terms of measure.

children.text: dve dve kāṣṭhe ca tasyordhvaṃ tadūrdhvaṃ tritayaṃ kṣipet // Rsk_1.25 //
children.translated_text: Then two pieces of wood above that, and above that three should be added. // Rsk_1.25 //
After two <s>yāmas</s> (six hours), one should remove the embers and the water.

children.text: ūrdhvasthālyāṃ tu yallagnaṃ tadūrdhvaṃ bhasma siddhidam // Rsk_1.26 //
children.translated_text: That which adheres to the upper pot — that upper [substance] is the <s>bhasma</s> (ash) that grants <s>siddhi</s> (success). // Rsk_1.26 //
Mercury: Production of Talabhasman (Bottom Ash)

children.text: gandhakaṃ dhūmasāraṃ ca śuddhasūtaṃ samaṃ trayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Gandhaka</s> (sulfur), <s>dhūmasāra</s> (sal ammoniac), and purified <s>sūta</s> (mercury) — the three in equal parts —

children.text: yāmaikaṃ mardayet khalve kācakūpyāṃ vinikṣipet // Rsk_1.27 //
children.translated_text: one should grind for one <s>yāma</s> (three hours) in a mortar and place into a glass flask. // Rsk_1.27 //
Having sealed it, one should cook it in a <s>vālukā-yantra</s> (sand-bath apparatus) for twelve <s>yāmas</s> (thirty-six hours).

children.text: sphoṭayetsvāṅgaśītaṃ ca tadūrdhvaṃ gandhakaṃ tyajet // Rsk_1.28 //
children.translated_text: After it cools on its own, one should break [the flask] open and discard the <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur) from the upper portion. // Rsk_1.28 //
Talabhasman: Medicinal Properties
<s>Talabhasma</s> (bottom ash) becomes <s>yogavāhī</s> (a carrier/potentiator of medicines) and destroys all diseases.
I shall describe the change of colors through combination with other medicines. // Rsk_1.29 //

body.text: raktaṃ pītaṃ tathā kṛṣṇaṃ nīlaṃ ca pāṇḍurāruṇam /
body.translated_text: Red, yellow, black, blue, and pale-reddish [are the colors].

children.translated_text: Combined with the juice of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo), mixed with <s>capala</s> (bismuth), // Rsk_1.30 //

body.translated_text: Red Bhasma
the <s>bhasma</s> (ash) becomes red in color, resembling the flower of a pomegranate.

children.text: bhūdhātrīhastiśuṇḍībhyāṃ rasaṃ gandhaṃ ca mardayet // Rsk_1.31 //
children.translated_text: With <s>bhūdhātrī</s> (Phyllanthus niruri) and <s>hastiśuṇḍī</s> (Heliotropium indicum), one should grind <s>rasa</s> (mercury) and <s>gandha</s> (sulfur). // Rsk_1.31 //

body.translated_text: Yellow Bhasma
Cooked in a glass flask for four <s>yāmas</s> (twelve hours), the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) becomes yellow.

children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) combined with <s>gandhaka</s> (sulfur), ground with the juice of <s>kumārī</s> (aloe vera), // Rsk_1.32 //

body.translated_text: Black Bhasma
the <s>bhasma</s> (ash) becomes black in color, rare even among the gods.

children.translated_text: Combined with the tuber of <s>vārāhī</s> (Dioscorea bulbifera), mixed with <s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore/calamine), // Rsk_1.33 //

body.translated_text: Dark Blue Bhasma
the <s>bhasma</s> (ash) becomes dark in color and destroys wrinkles and grey hair.

children.translated_text: In a flask coated inside with salt, [the bhasma] becomes pale-reddish. // Rsk_1.34 //

body.translated_text: Pale Reddish Bhasma

children.translated_text: Mercury: Māraṇa (Calcination/Killing)
Twenty parts of salt and one part of <s>sūta</s> (mercury);

children.text: kāñjike mardayitvāgnau puṭanād bhasmatāṃ vrajet // Rsk_1.35 //
children.translated_text: having ground [them] in <s>kāñjika</s> (sour gruel) and heating in a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed crucible furnace), it attains the state of <s>bhasma</s> (ash). // Rsk_1.35 //
Removing [the salt], adding fresh <s>rasa</s> (mercury), one may calcine the mercury as desired.
In this manner, copper, lead, tin, and mica, when calcined, become efficacious. // Rsk_1.36 //
That [bhasma] should be placed gently in a vessel filled with water for eight <s>yāmas</s> (twenty-four hours).

children.text: tyaktvā toyaṃ raso grāhyaḥ pātrastho bhasmasūtakaḥ // Rsk_1.37 //
children.translated_text: Discarding the water, the <s>rasa</s> (mercury) remaining in the vessel — the <s>bhasmasūtaka</s> (calcined mercury) — should be collected. // Rsk_1.37 //
Mercury: Māraṇa (Calcination — Another Method)
One should prepare a pair of crucibles with the powdered seeds of <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera).
<s>Pārada</s> (mercury), placed in that <s>puṭa</s> (crucible), ground with the juice of <s>malayūra</s> (a type of citrus), // Rsk_1.38 //
flowers of <s>droṇapuṣpī</s> (Leucas cephalotes), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia ribes), and <s>arimedaka</s> (a medicinal plant) —

children.text: cūrṇam eṣām adhaścordhvaṃ dattvā mudrāṃ prakalpayet // Rsk_1.39 //
children.translated_text: having placed the powder of these below and above, one should prepare the seal. // Rsk_1.39 //
Having properly formed a ball, one should place it in a <s>sampuṭa</s> (sealed pair) of earthen crucibles.

children.text: śoṣayenmudritaṃ kṛtvā paced gajapuṭe tataḥ // Rsk_1.40 //
children.translated_text: After drying and sealing, one should then heat it in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-sized pit furnace). // Rsk_1.40 //
<s>Pārada</s> (mercury) thus attains the state of <s>bhasma</s> (ash) with a single <s>puṭa</s> (heating cycle).
After it has cooled on its own, one should remove it and employ it in all [therapeutic] procedures. // Rsk_1.41 //
In an inverted shallow vessel on the furnace, coated with <s>sphaṭikā</s> (alum), one should place [the mercury].
Cooked in the juice of <s>punarnavā</s> (Boerhavia diffusa), <s>rasa</s> (mercury) dies through grinding. // Rsk_1.42 //
Mercury: Test for Proper Calcination (Mṛta-parīkṣā)

children.text: atejā aguruḥ śubhro lohahā cācalo rasaḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>rasa</s> (mercury) is lusterless, light, bright white, capable of absorbing metals, and immobile,

children.text: yadā nāvartate vahnau nordhvaṃ gacchettadā mṛtaḥ // Rsk_1.43 //
children.translated_text: when it does not revert in fire and does not rise upward — then it is [truly] dead (calcined). // Rsk_1.43 //
Calcined Mercury: Medicinal Properties
<s>Pārada</s> (mercury) destroys all diseases, is <s>yogavāhī</s> (a potentiator of medicines), fluid, and heavy.
It destroys <s>pāṇḍutā</s> (anemia), <s>kṛmi</s> (worms), and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (skin diseases); it is an aphrodisiac, a strengthener, and a <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenative). // Rsk_1.44 //

body.text: sūto dhāturasāḥ sarve jīrṇā jīrṇā guṇādhikāḥ /
body.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) and all <s>dhāturasas</s> (metallic preparations), the more they are digested, the greater their qualities become.

children.text: dante śṛṅge maṇau veṇau rakṣayetsādhitaṃ rasam // Rsk_1.45 //
children.translated_text: One should store the processed <s>rasa</s> (mercury) in [containers made of] ivory, horn, gemstone, or bamboo. // Rsk_1.45 //

body.translated_text: Storage of Calcined Mercury

children.translated_text: Dosage Weights of Drugs
For <s>pitta</s> (bile-based preparations), one-sixteenth part; for poisons, one <s>raktikā</s> (unit of weight).
Even when not explicitly stated for <s>guṭī</s> (pills) and <s>rasas</s> (mercurial preparations), this rule should be understood by itself. // Rsk_1.46 //
Mercury: Administration (Sevana)
For the destruction of all diseases and for the purpose of strengthening the body,
one whose body is purified and who follows a proper diet should consume [mercury] after worshipping the deity. // Rsk_1.47 //

children.text: vallamekaṃ nare'śve tu gadyāṇaṃ ca gaje dvayam /
children.translated_text: One <s>valla</s> (a unit of weight) for a human, one <s>gadyāṇa</s> for a horse, and two [<s>gadyāṇas</s>] for an elephant;

children.text: dattaḥ sūto haredrogān dhātuyugvā nijauṣadhaiḥ // Rsk_1.48 //
children.translated_text: <s>sūta</s> (mercury) so administered removes diseases, or [it may be given] with <s>dhātuyug</s> (paired metals) along with their respective medicines. // Rsk_1.48 //

children.text: rasasya vikṛtau satyāṃ mūrchā hikkā jvaro'ratiḥ /
children.translated_text: When adverse reactions to <s>rasa</s> (mercury) occur — fainting, hiccups, fever, restlessness —

children.text: kāsaḥ śvāso bhramo moho dāhaḥ kampaśca jāyate // Rsk_1.49 //
children.translated_text: Cough, dyspnea, dizziness, stupor, burning sensation, and trembling arise. // Rsk_1.49 //

children.text: tacchāntyai bījapūrasya rasaṃ śuṇṭhīṃ ca saindhavam /
children.translated_text: For its pacification, the juice of citron (<s>bījapūra</s>), dry ginger (<s>śuṇṭhī</s>), and rock salt (<s>saindhava</s>)

children.text: pibedvā gojale siddhaṃ mūlaṃ karkoṭajaṃ śubham // Rsk_1.50 //
children.translated_text: should be drunk; or the auspicious root of <s>karkoṭa</s> (spiny gourd), cooked in cow's urine. // Rsk_1.50 //
In the household where the lord of mercury (<s>rasādhīśa</s>) is worshipped with great devotion,
that [household] is filled with progeny and wealth, and free from mental and physical afflictions (<s>ādhi</s> and <s>vyādhi</s>). // Rsk_1.51 //

body.translated_text: RSK, 2

[The Six Metals]
The six metals are declared to be gold (<s>hema</s>), silver (<s>rūpya</s>), copper (<s>arka</s>), tin (<s>vaṅga</s>), lead (<s>āhi</s>), and iron (<s>loha</s>).

children.translated_text: These [six] are natural; <s>ghoṣāvartaka</s> and others are artificial. // Rsk_2.1 //

body.translated_text: [Metals: Factitious]

body.text:
<metals:: śuddha, mṛta:: medic. properties>
śuddhā mṛtā nirutthāśca sarvarogaharāḥ smṛtāḥ /
body.translated_text:
[Metals: Purified, Calcined — Medicinal Properties]
Those that are purified (<s>śuddha</s>), calcined (<s>mṛta</s>), and non-resurgent (<s>niruttha</s>) are said to cure all diseases.

children.translated_text: One should discard those that are impure and insufficiently processed, as they cause disease and death. // Rsk_2.2 //

body.translated_text: [Metals: Impure — Medicinal Properties]

children.translated_text: [Metals: Calcination with Mercury]
A metal combined with mercury (<s>sūta</s>) abandons its defects, and mercury combined with metal

children.text: ataḥ svarṇādilohāni vinā sūtaṃ na mārayet // Rsk_2.3 //
children.translated_text: [likewise abandons its defects]; therefore one should not calcine gold and other metals without mercury. // Rsk_2.3 //
[Gold: Subtypes]
Gold (<s>svarṇa</s>) is said to be of five types: natural (<s>prākṛta</s>), innate (<s>sahaja</s>), fire-born (<s>āgneya</s>),
these three types of gold are fit for the gods, of sixteen <s>varṇa</s> (carats). // Rsk_2.4 //
Mineral (<s>khanija</s>) and alchemically produced (<s>rasavādottha</s>), having been well-leafed and purified,
that is of fourteen <s>varṇa</s> (carats), fit for humans, and removes disease. // Rsk_2.5 //

body.text:
<gold:: śodhana>
suvarṇaṃ saptaśo vāpyaṃ kāñcanārarase śuciḥ /
body.translated_text:
[Gold: Purification]
Gold should be quenched seven times in the juice of <s>kāñcanāra</s> (Bauhinia variegata) to become pure.

children.text: suvarṇe galite nāgaṃ prakṣipet ṣoḍaśāṃśakam // Rsk_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Into molten gold, one should add lead (<s>nāga</s>) to the extent of one-sixteenth. // Rsk_2.6 //

body.translated_text: [Gold: Calcination]

children.text: amlena mardayitvā tu kṛtvā tasya ca golakam /
children.translated_text: Having ground it with acid and made it into a ball,
placing sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) equal to the ball, one above and one below, // Rsk_2.7 //
placing in a saucer-sealed vessel (<s>śarāvasaṃpuṭa</s>) and sealing it, one should heat it.
With fire fueled by thirty cow-dung cakes (<s>vanotpala</s>), repeated seven times, it becomes ash (<s>bhasma</s>). // Rsk_2.8 //
[Gold: Calcined — Medicinal Properties]
It is bitter, astringent, fever-curing, sweet in post-digestive effect (<s>vipāka</s>), and strength-giving,
bestowing longevity, intelligence, and beauty, aphrodisiac (<s>vṛṣya</s>), and removing consumption, misfortune, and poison. // Rsk_2.9 //
[Silver: Subtypes]

children.text: kailāse sahajaṃ rūpyaṃ khanijaṃ kṛtrimaṃ bhuvi /
children.translated_text: Silver (<s>rūpya</s>) is innate (<s>sahaja</s>) on Mount <s>Kailāsa</s>, mineral (<s>khanija</s>) and artificial (<s>kṛtrima</s>) on earth.

children.text: vyutkrameṇa guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ nāgottīrṇaṃ rase hitam // Rsk_2.10 //
children.translated_text: In reverse order they are superior in qualities; that which has been freed from lead (<s>nāga</s>) is beneficial in mercurial preparations. // Rsk_2.10 //

body.translated_text:
[Silver: Purification]
Silver should be purified in the juice of white <s>Agasti</s> (Sesbania grandiflora), like gold. Its calcination:

children.translated_text: with a combination of sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) and acid, removing lead (<s>nāga</s>), one should add tin (<s>trapu</s>). // Rsk_2.11 //

body.translated_text: [Silver: Calcination]
It promotes longevity, semen, strength, and vitality, and removes all diseases.

children.translated_text: When this ash, smeared on a blade with acid, produces a copper color, then it is properly calcined (<s>mṛta</s>). // Rsk_2.12 //

body.translated_text: [Gold, Silver: Test for Calcination]

children.text: suvarṇamathavā rūpyaṃ yoge yatra na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Where gold or silver is not available in a formulation,

children.text: tatra kāntodbhavaṃ lohaṃ kṣepyaṃ taistatsamaṃ guṇaiḥ // Rsk_2.13 //
children.translated_text: there one should use iron derived from a magnet (<s>kāntaloha</s>), as it is equal to them in qualities. // Rsk_2.13 //

body.text:
<copper:: subtypes>
dvyarkau nepālamlecchau tu rase nepāla uttamaḥ /
body.translated_text:
[Copper: Subtypes]
Copper is of two types: <s>Nepāla</s> and <s>Mleccha</s>; in mercurial preparations, <s>Nepāla</s> is superior.

children.translated_text: It withstands hammering, is unctuous, red-leafed, clean, and soft. // Rsk_2.14 //

body.translated_text: [Nepāla Copper: Physical Properties]

children.translated_text: [Mleccha Copper: Physical Properties]

children.text: mlecchastu kṣālitaḥ kṛṣṇo rūkṣaḥ stabdho ghanāsahaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Mleccha</s> [copper], when washed, is black, rough, rigid, and unable to withstand hammering.

children.text: miśrito nāgalohābhyāṃ na śreṣṭho rasakarmaṇi // Rsk_2.15 //
children.translated_text: Mixed with lead and iron, it is not suitable for mercurial operations. // Rsk_2.15 //
[Copper: Defects]

children.text: tāmraṃ tu viṣavajjñeyaṃ yatnataḥ sādhyate hi tat /
children.translated_text: Copper should be known as [potent] like poison; it must be processed with great care.

children.text: eko doṣo viṣe samyaktāmre tvaṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ // Rsk_2.16 //
children.translated_text: Poison has one defect, while copper is declared to have eight. // Rsk_2.16 //
Skin disease (<s>kuṣṭha</s>), purging, vomiting, delusion, burning, wind disorders (<s>vāta</s>), and jaundice (<s>kāmalā</s>),

children.text: dehasya nāśanaṃ doṣā ityaṣṭau kathitā budhaiḥ // Rsk_2.17 //
children.translated_text: and destruction of the body — these eight defects are declared by the wise. // Rsk_2.17 //
[Copper: Purification]
One should cook copper leaf for a day in cow's urine over a strong fire,
then wash it with water; [repeated] twenty-one times, it becomes pure. // Rsk_2.18 //
[Copper: Calcination]
One should grind mercury (<s>pārada</s>), sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), and copper in equal parts with acid.
Ash is produced from three firings (<s>tripuṭa</s>), or alternatively from a sand-bath apparatus (<s>vālukāyantra</s>). // Rsk_2.19 //
[Copper: Calcination]
Sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) in two parts and copper (<s>arka</s>) in one part should be fired in a saucer-sealed vessel (<s>śarāvasaṃpuṭa</s>).

children.text: svāṅgaśītaṃ ca saṃpeṣya khalve vastreṇa gālayet // Rsk_2.20 //
children.translated_text: When self-cooled, grind it in a mortar and filter through cloth. // Rsk_2.20 //
Adding sea salt (<s>sāmudra</s>) in equal quantity, one should fire it again.

children.text: tadeva tatkṣaye deyaṃ sāmudraṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ // Rsk_2.21 //
children.translated_text: As it diminishes, the same sea salt should be added again and again. // Rsk_2.21 //

children.text: kāsīsasya jalenaiva vāraṃ vāraṃ tu bhāvayet /
children.translated_text: One should triturate it repeatedly with a solution of green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>).
With sixty-four firings in this manner, it becomes non-resurgent (<s>niruttha</s>) and a carrier for formulations (<s>yogavāhika</s>). // Rsk_2.22 //
That copper should be fired with <s>sauraṇa</s> bulb or with <s>pañcāmṛta</s> (the five nectars),

children.text: aṣṭau doṣāṃśca pūrvoktān na karoti guṇāvaham // Rsk_2.23 //
children.translated_text: it does not produce the eight previously mentioned defects and is beneficial in qualities. // Rsk_2.23 //
It destroys abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), consumption (<s>kṣaya</s>), indigestion (<s>ajīrṇa</s>), cough (<s>kāsa</s>), anemia (<s>pāṇḍu</s>), and fevers.
It is excellent for obesity (<s>sthaulya</s>), abdominal enlargement (<s>udara</s>), phlegm (<s>kapha</s>), colic (<s>śūla</s>), and purification of upper and lower passages. // Rsk_2.24 //
[Tin: Subtypes]
Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) is said to be of two types: <s>khuraka</s> and <s>miśraka</s>.

children.text: khurakaṃ tu guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ miśrakaṃ na rase hitam // Rsk_2.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Khuraka</s> is superior in qualities; <s>miśraka</s> is not beneficial in mercurial preparations. // Rsk_2.25 //
[Tin: Purification]
Tin (<s>vaṅga</s>) and lead (<s>nāga</s>) should be purified twenty-one times in the juice of <s>kanyā</s> (aloe) and <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (Eclipta prostrata),
or in a decoction derived from <s>brahmavṛkṣa</s> (Butea monosperma), or from <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo). // Rsk_2.26 //
[Tin: Calcination]
When tin is melted in an earthen vessel, the powder of bark of tamarind (<s>ciñcā</s>) and sacred fig (<s>aśvattha</s>)
should be added to the extent of one-fourth, and stirred with an iron ladle. // Rsk_2.27 //
Until it becomes ash; then in a mortar with orpiment (<s>tālaka</s>),
it should be ground with the decoction and paste of <s>brahmadru</s> (Butea monosperma) and fired in <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-fire). // Rsk_2.28 //

children.text: puṭe puṭe daśāṃśāṃśaṃ dattvaivaṃ daśadhā puṭet /
children.translated_text: Adding one-tenth at each firing, one should fire it thus ten times.
That tin ash becomes non-resurgent (<s>niruttha</s>) and removes anemia (<s>pāṇḍu</s>) and urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>). // Rsk_2.29 //
[Tin: Calcination]
A tin leaf in a cow-dung sealed vessel (<s>karīṣasaṃpuṭa</s>), combined with goat dung,

children.text: mriyate puṭamātreṇa tanmehān hanti viṃśatim // Rsk_2.30 //
children.translated_text: becomes calcined in a single firing; it destroys twenty types of urinary diseases (<s>meha</s>). // Rsk_2.30 //
[Lead: Calcination]
Lead ash, prepared like tin — first adding realgar (<s>śilā</s>) equal to it,

children.text: kṣiptvā tuṣodakairmardyaṃ dadyād gajapuṭaṃ tataḥ // Rsk_2.31 //
children.translated_text: and grinding with husk-water (<s>tuṣodaka</s>), one should then give it <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-fire). // Rsk_2.31 //
Adding sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>) to one-sixtieth, it should be fired up to sixty firings.
That lead ash becomes non-resurgent and is superior in qualities to tin ash. // Rsk_2.32 //
[Lead, Tin: Calcined — Medicinal Properties]

children.text: mṛtaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca nāgaṃ ca rasabhasma samaṃ guṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Calcined tin and lead are equal in qualities to mercury ash (<s>rasabhasma</s>).
And when one is not available, one may substitute the other. // Rsk_2.33 //

body.text:
<iron:: subtypes>
muṇḍaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tathā kāntaṃ bhedāstasya trayodaśāḥ /
body.translated_text:
[Iron: Subtypes]
<s>Muṇḍa</s>, <s>tīkṣṇa</s>, and <s>kānta</s> (magnetic) — its varieties are thirteen.

children.text: mṛdu kuṇṭhaṃ ca kāṇḍāraṃ trividhaṃ muṇḍamucyate // Rsk_2.34 //
children.translated_text: <s>Muṇḍa</s> is said to be of three types: <s>mṛdu</s> (soft), <s>kuṇṭha</s> (blunt), and <s>kāṇḍāra</s>. // Rsk_2.34 //

body.translated_text: [Muṇḍa: Subtypes]

children.translated_text: [Tīkṣṇaloha: Subtypes]

children.text: kharasāraṃ ca hotrāsaṃ tārāvartaṃ viḍaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Kharasāra</s>, <s>hotrāsa</s>, <s>tārāvarta</s>, <s>viḍa</s>,

children.text: kāntaṃ lohaṃ gajākhyaṃ ca ṣaḍvidhaṃ tīkṣṇamucyate // Rsk_2.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>kānta</s> iron, and that called <s>gaja</s> (elephant) — <s>tīkṣṇa</s> is said to be of six types. // Rsk_2.35 //
[Kānta Iron: Test]

children.text: pātre yasminprasarati jale tailabindurna lipto hiṅgurgandhaṃ visṛjati nijaṃ tiktatāṃ nimbakalkaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the vessel where it is placed, a drop of oil spreads on water without being applied, asafoetida (<s>hiṅgu</s>) releases its own fragrance, neem (<s>nimba</s>) paste [releases] its bitterness,

children.text: pāke dugdhaṃ bhavati śikharākāratāṃ naiti bhūmau kāntaṃ lohaṃ tadidamuditaṃ lakṣaṇairnaiva cānyat // Rsk_2.36 //
children.translated_text: in cooking, milk forms a peak-like shape and does not spread on the ground — that is magnetic iron (<s>kāntaloha</s>), declared by these characteristics and none other. // Rsk_2.36 //
[Kānta Iron: Subtypes]

children.text: kāntaṃ lohaṃ caturdhoktaṃ romakaṃ bhrāmakaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: Magnetic iron (<s>kāntaloha</s>) is said to be of four types: <s>romaka</s>, <s>bhrāmaka</s>,
<s>cumbaka</s>, and <s>drāvaka</s> — their qualities are progressively superior. // Rsk_2.37 //

body.translated_text:
[Iron: Purification]
The wise person should purify all irons beginning with <s>muṇḍa</s> in the same manner as copper.

children.translated_text: [Iron: Processing]
The processing (<s>pāka</s>) of iron is declared to be of three degrees: soft (<s>mṛdu</s>), medium (<s>madhya</s>), and hard (<s>khara</s>).
The first two are of muddy and dry appearance respectively, while the hard stage resembles sand. // Rsk_2.38 //
[Iron: Calcination]

children.text: lohapatraṃ gandhaliptaṃ vahnau taptaṃ punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: An iron leaf smeared with sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>), heated in fire again and again,
should be plunged into the juice of <s>mīnākṣikā</s> (Luffa acutangula) until it crumbles therein. // Rsk_2.39 //
That should be ground firmly with equal parts of mercury (<s>rasa</s>), cinnabar (<s>hiṅgula</s>), and sulphur (<s>gandhaka</s>).

With the juices of <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex negundo), <s>vṛṣa</s> (Adhatoda vasica), and <s>matsyākṣī</s> (Alternanthera sessilis), calcination is achieved through <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-fire). // Rsk_2.40 //
[Iron: Calcination — Water-Floating Test]

children.text: lohacūrṇaṃ varākvāthe piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Iron powder, made into a lump with a decoction of <s>varā</s> (Terminalia chebula) again and again,
should be fired in a windless pit of sixteen finger-breadths measurement. // Rsk_2.41 //
With sixty-four firings, it becomes like a ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>).
Non-resurgent (<s>niruttha</s>), water-floating (<s>ambutara</s>), and a carrier for formulations (<s>yogavāhi</s>), it cures all diseases. // Rsk_2.42 //
[Iron: Calcination — Water-Floating Test]
In the juice of <s>jambū</s> bark (Syzygium cumini), or in that produced from <s>tindu</s> and <s>mārkaṇḍa</s> leaves,

children.text: trisaptadhātape śoṣyaṃ peṣyaṃ vāritaraṃ bhavet // Rsk_2.43 //
children.translated_text: it should be dried in the sun twenty-one times and ground; it becomes water-floating (<s>vāritara</s>). // Rsk_2.43 //
[Iron: Calcination]
An iron leaf, thin as a tamarind (<s>ciñcā</s>) leaf, should be placed in the juice of <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum montanum).

children.text: gharme dhṛtvā raso deyo mṛtaṃ yāvadbhavecca tat // Rsk_2.44 //
children.translated_text: Keeping it in the sun, mercury (<s>rasa</s>) should be applied until it becomes calcined. // Rsk_2.44 //
[Iron: Calcination — Water-Floating Test]
One should place an iron leaf in the midst of <s>matsyākṣī</s> (Alternanthera sessilis) juice.

children.text: triṃśaddināni gharme tu tato vāritaraṃ bhavet // Rsk_2.45 //
children.translated_text: for thirty days in summer, then it should become water-quenched. // Rsk_2.45 //
<iron:: calcination:: <s>niruttha</s> (completely killed), test>
If iron combined with honey and ghee, [heated with] silver,

children.text: tadā lohaṃ nirutthaṃ syādanyathā sādhayetpunaḥ // Rsk_2.46 //
children.translated_text: when smelted retains its original measure, then the iron is <s>niruttha</s> (completely killed); otherwise, one should process it again. // Rsk_2.46 //
<iron:: <s>amṛtīkaraṇa</s> (making immortal) (?)>
In a decoction of <s>Varā</s> (Terminalia chebula), the remaining amount of ghee equal to the iron,

children.text: sitā lohamitā tāmre pakvaṃ cāmṛtavadbhavet // Rsk_2.47 //
children.translated_text: sugar equal to the iron — cooked in a copper vessel, it becomes like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar). // Rsk_2.47 //
<iron:: calcined:: medicinal properties>
<s>Grahaṇī</s> (sprue), <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia), <s>śopha</s> (swelling), <s>arśas</s> (hemorrhoids), <s>jvara</s> (fever), <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumors), <s>prameha</s> (urinary diseases) —
iron destroys these and also splenic disease; it increases strength and intelligence. // Rsk_2.48 //

children.text: kuṣmāṇḍaṃ tilatailaṃ ca māṣānnaṃ rājikā tathā /
children.translated_text: Ash gourd, sesame oil, black gram food, mustard,
wine, and sour substances — one who takes iron should avoid these. // Rsk_2.49 //
<<s>maṇḍūra</s> (iron rust):: purification>
Heated in cow's urine and <s>triphalā</s> decoction, it should be purified twenty-one times.
The slag (<s>kiṭṭa</s>) of gold and all other metals carries the properties of that respective metal. // Rsk_2.50 //
Iron-rust (<s>muṇḍa</s>) is ten times [more potent] than slag; <s>tīkṣṇa</s> (steel) is a hundred times more than iron-rust;
<s>kānta</s> (magnetic iron) is a hundred thousand times more than steel — when consumed, it produces [these] benefits. // Rsk_2.51 //
<<s>rasaka</s> (zinc ore):: calcination>
The essence (<s>sattva</s>) derived from <s>kharpara</s> (zinc ore), placed inside salt in a vessel,

children.text: sukhaṃ ruddhvā vipakvaṃ tanmriyate gajavahninā // Rsk_2.52 //
children.translated_text: well-sealed and cooked, is killed by <s>gajavahni</s> (elephant-fire, a strong fire). // Rsk_2.52 //
<<s>rasaka</s>:: calcined:: medicinal properties>
Calcined <s>rasaka</s> is dry, destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>, and removes fever;
it is a <s>yogavāhī</s> (synergistic carrier), destroys diarrhea, eliminates moisture, and causes constipation. // Rsk_2.53 //
<bronze, brass:: purification, calcination>
For bronze and brass, the purification and calcination are declared to be the same as for copper;
sugar mixed with cow products should be given for ill effects from consuming metals. // Rsk_2.54 //
<metals:: rapid calcination>
Now, one part of mercury, then double that of sulfur,
equal amounts of both with gold and other <s>niruttha</s> (killed) metals — this is rapid calcination. // Rsk_2.55 //
<metals:: <s>niruttha</s> (completely killed):: test>
Metals calcined with equal [parts of] honey, ghee, and borax, and with a <s>guñjā</s>-weight of jaggery,

children.text: dhmātāḥ piṇḍakṛtā naiva jīvanti te nirutthakāḥ // Rsk_2.56 //
children.translated_text: when smelted do not form a lump — they are <s>niruttha</s> (completely killed). // Rsk_2.56 //
<metal:: calcination:: <s>niruttha</s> (completely killed)>
A metal that has risen with sulfur should be ground in the juice of aloe for a day;

children.text: pakvo gajapuṭo divyaṃ sarvo yāti nirutthatām // Rsk_2.57 //
children.translated_text: cooked in an elephant-fire pit, every [metal] attains the state of being <s>niruttha</s> (completely killed). // Rsk_2.57 //
<<s>abhra</s> (mica):: subtypes>
<s>Abhra</s> (mica) is of four kinds, each being yellow, white-black, or red:

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajraṃ cāgnau parīkṣayet // Rsk_2.58 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pināka</s>, <s>Dardura</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, and <s>Vajra</s> — one should test them in fire. // Rsk_2.58 //

body.text:
<abhra:: vajra>
na patrāṇi na śabdāṃśca kuryāttadvajrasaṃjñakam /
body.translated_text:
<<s>abhra</s>:: <s>vajra</s> type>
That which produces neither flakes nor sounds is designated <s>vajra</s> (diamond-mica).

children.text: trīṇi dhmātāni kiṭṭaṃ hi vajrī sattvaṃ vimuñcati // Rsk_2.59 //
children.translated_text: Smelted three times, the <s>vajra</s>-mica releases its essence, [leaving behind] slag. // Rsk_2.59 //

body.translated_text: <<s>abhra</s>:: <s>vajra</s>:: extraction of essence>

children.translated_text: <<s>abhra</s>:: <s>vajra</s>:: essence:: calcination>

children.text: tatsattvaṃ vidhivadgrāhyaṃ śodhyaṃ māryaṃ ca lohavat /
children.translated_text: That essence should be collected methodically, purified, and calcined like metal;

children.text: sattvābhāve tu niścandraṃ raseṣviṣṭaṃ taducyate // Rsk_2.60 //
children.translated_text: in the absence of essence, moon-less [mica] (<s>niścandra</s>) is desired in mercurial preparations — so it is said. // Rsk_2.60 //
<<s>abhra</s>:: calcination:: production of <s>niścandra</s> (lustreless mica)>

children.text: dhānyābhraṃ meghanādair jhaṣanayanajalair jambhalaiṣṭaṅkaṇena khalve saṃmardya gāḍhaṃ tadanu gajapuṭān dvādaśaivaṃ pradadyāt /
children.translated_text: Grinding <s>abhra</s> (mica) thoroughly in a mortar with grain-liquor, <s>meghanāda</s> (Eclipta), fish-eye juices, <s>jambha</s> (lime), and borax, one should then give twelve elephant-fire pits;

children.text: mīnākṣībhṛṅgatoyais triphalajalayutair mardayet saptarātraṃ gandhaṃ tulyaṃ ca dattvā pravaragajapuṭāt pañcatāṃ yāti cābhram // Rsk_2.61 //
children.translated_text: grinding for seven nights with <s>mīnākṣī</s> (Eclipta) and <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta alba) waters mixed with <s>triphalā</s> water, and adding an equal amount of sulfur, the mica dies from an excellent elephant-fire pit. // Rsk_2.61 //
<<s>abhra</s>:: <s>niścandra</s> (lustreless):: medicinal properties>
Calcined mica that has become lustreless (<s>niścandra</s>) and tawny is comparable to nectar;
mica with luster (<s>sacandra</s>) should be known as poisonous, causing death like tiger's hair. // Rsk_2.62 //
<<s>abhra</s>:: <s>amṛtīkaraṇa</s> (making immortal)>
<s>Varā</s> (Terminalia chebula) water, cow's ghee, and mica in the ratio of one-sixth-ten proportions,
cooked on a gentle fire in an iron vessel — this constitutes the <s>amṛtīkaraṇa</s> (immortalization process). // Rsk_2.63 //
<<s>abhra</s>:: calcined:: medicinal properties>
It arrests aging, removes old age and death, sustains strength and health, and destroys great skin diseases;

children.text: mṛto meghakaḥ sarvarogeṣu yojyaḥ sadā sūtarājasya vīryeṇa tulyaḥ // Rsk_2.64 //
children.translated_text: calcined mica should be employed in all diseases; its potency is always equal to that of <s>sūtarāja</s> (mercury, the king of essences). // Rsk_2.64 //
Alkalis, sour substances, pulses, <s>karkoṭikā</s> (spiny gourd), <s>karavellaka</s> (bitter gourd),

children.text: vṛntākaṃ ca karīraṃ ca tailaṃ cābhrakasevane // Rsk_2.65 //
children.translated_text: eggplant, <s>karīra</s> (caper), and oil should be avoided while taking mica. // Rsk_2.65 //

body.translated_text: RSK, 3

children.translated_text: <<s>mahārasa</s> (great essences):: purification>
Sulfur and arsenic compounds should be purified in Nepal [cow's] milk; <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch)

children.text: gomūtreṇa ca tālādyaṃ śaṅkhādyam amlataḥ śuciḥ // Rsk_3.1 //
children.translated_text: in cow's urine; and <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) and the like should be purified with sour substances, and <s>śaṅkha</s> (conch) and the like become pure [thereby]. // Rsk_3.1 //
<<s>viṣa</s> (poison):: calcination>
<s>Viṣa</s> (poison, i.e. aconite) as stated in mercurial texts should be taken, ground with an equal amount of borax;

children.text: tanmṛtaṃ yogavāhi syāt sūtābhrāyaḥ samaṃ guṇaiḥ // Rsk_3.2 //
children.translated_text: when calcined it becomes a <s>yogavāhī</s> (synergistic carrier), equal in properties to mercury, mica, and iron. // Rsk_3.2 //
<<s>viṣa</s>:: mantras>
Poison consecrated seven times with the mantra called <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> (Blue-throated <s>Śiva</s>)

children.text: auṣadhe ca rase caiva dātavyaṃ hitamicchatā // Rsk_3.3 //
children.translated_text: should be administered in medicine and in mercurial preparations by one who desires benefit. // Rsk_3.3 //
<<s>viṣa</s>:: medicinal use>

children.text: nānārasauṣadhairye tu duṣṭā yāntīha no gadāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those diseases that do not yield to various essences and medicines,

children.text: te naśyanti viṣe datte śīghraṃ vātakaphodbhavāḥ // Rsk_3.4 //
children.translated_text: they are destroyed quickly when poison is administered, especially those arising from <s>vāta</s> (wind) and <s>kapha</s> (phlegm). // Rsk_3.4 //
<<s>viṣa</s>:: dosage>
The best, medium, and lowest doses are eight, six, and four <s>yava</s>-grains [respectively];

children.text: atimātraṃ yadā bhuktaṃ tadājyaṭaṅkaṇe pibet // Rsk_3.5 //
children.translated_text: when taken in excess, one should drink ghee and borax. // Rsk_3.5 //

children.text: rajanīṃ meghanādaṃ vā sarpākṣīṃ vā ghṛtānvitām /
children.translated_text: Or <s>rajanī</s> (turmeric), or <s>meghanāda</s> (Eclipta), or <s>sarpākṣī</s> (snake-eye plant) mixed with ghee;
or one should lick powdered <s>Arjuna</s> bark with honey and ghee. // Rsk_3.6 //

children.text: na deyaṃ krodhine klībe pittārte rājayakṣmiṇi /
children.translated_text: It should not be given to one who is angry, impotent, afflicted with <s>pitta</s> (bile), suffering from <s>rājayakṣma</s> (consumption),
or to one suffering from hunger, thirst, vertigo, heat, or travel, nor to one who is emaciated and ill. // Rsk_3.7 //
Poison should not be [given] to pregnant women, children, or the elderly, nor in the royal palace;
it should be given to one devoted to rejuvenation therapy, who eats food accompanied by ghee and milk. // Rsk_3.8 //
<<s>upaviṣa</s> (sub-poisons)>
<s>Lāṅgalī</s>, <s>Vajrī</s>, <s>Hemārka</s>, <s>Hayāri</s>, <s>Viṣamuṣṭikā</s> —
these are called <s>upaviṣas</s> (sub-poisons); they are used in mercurial operations. // Rsk_3.9 //
<<s>ahiphena</s> (opium):: mythological origin>
When the ocean was being churned, from the mouth of <s>Vāsuki</s> flowed rapidly
a mass of foam, which, due to agitation and hissing, fell upon the earth. // Rsk_3.10 //
<<s>ahiphena</s>:: medicinal properties>
Therefore it is called <s>ahiphena</s> (serpent-foam, i.e. opium); it is bitter, astringent, and desiccating;
it causes stupor, destroys asthma and cough; once used, it is impossible to abandon. // Rsk_3.11 //
It destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm), produces <s>vāta</s> (wind); when properly used, that poison becomes nectar;
it causes firmness of virility in men and bestows pleasure upon women. // Rsk_3.12 //
<<s>siddhamūlī</s>:: mythological origin>
In ancient times, the ocean of gems was churned by gods and demons;

children.text: tasmādamṛtamutpannaṃ devaiḥ pītaṃ na dānavaiḥ // Rsk_3.13 //
children.translated_text: from that arose <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), which was drunk by the gods but not by the <s>dānavas</s> (demons). // Rsk_3.13 //
Then from the hand of <s>Dhanvantari</s>, nectar fell upon the earth;

children.text: tasmin sarvairlehyamāne darbhair jihvā dvidhā kṛtā // Rsk_3.14 //
children.translated_text: as everyone was licking it up, the tongue was split in two by <s>darbha</s> grass. // Rsk_3.14 //

body.translated_text: Born from the blood and poison of the tongue, <s>siddhamūlī</s> is a great medicinal herb.

children.text: sā caturdhā sitā raktā pītā kṛṣṇā prasūnakaiḥ // Rsk_3.15 //
children.translated_text: It is of four kinds — white, red, yellow, and black — [distinguished] by their flowers. // Rsk_3.15 //

body.translated_text: <<s>siddhamūlī</s>:: colors>

children.translated_text: <<s>siddhamūlī</s>:: medicinal properties>

children.text: āhlādinī buddhirūpā yoge mantre ca siddhidā /
children.translated_text: It is delighting, of the nature of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), grants success in <s>yoga</s> and <s>mantra</s>;
it removes all diseases, arouses desire, and stimulates hunger. // Rsk_3.16 //
RSK, 4
Now certain preparations (<s>rasas</s>) that produce conviction will be described,
as received from the tradition, from the teacher's mouth, and from examining the treatises. // Rsk_4.1 //
Mercury, <s>rasaka</s> (zinc), orpiment, copper sulfate, sulfur, and borax —
all these in equal amounts, purified, should be ground for one day with the juices of <s>kāravellī</s> (bitter gourd). // Rsk_4.2 //
With that, one should coat the interior of a copper vessel thickly,
to a thickness of half a finger-width, and cook it in a sand-bath. // Rsk_4.3 //
In the apparatus, until rice grains burst on its surface,
then, when fully cooled, the wise should collect [the sublimate] from inside the copper vessel. // Rsk_4.4 //
Adding an equal amount of pepper and powdering everything together,

children.text: dviguñjaṃ parṇakhaṇḍena vātike paittike jvare // Rsk_4.5 //
children.translated_text: two <s>guñjā</s>-weights in a betel leaf for <s>vātika</s> (wind-type) and <s>paittika</s> (bile-type) fever; // Rsk_4.5 //
one <s>guñjā</s>-weight with sugar should be given; three <s>guñjā</s>-weights with <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents) for phlegm-type [fever];
in <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined-type) fever, it should be given with <s>vallī</s> (Piper longum) decoction and ginger juice. // Rsk_4.6 //
Within three days, it destroys irregular, severe, quotidian, tertian, and quartan fevers —
this preparation called <s>Śītabhañjī</s> (Cold-Destroyer) was created by <s>Rudra</s> (Śiva). // Rsk_4.7 //

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ śilāṃ tālaṃ saṃmathya nimbujairdravaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulfur, realgar, and orpiment — grinding with lemon juice,

children.text: liptvā tanvarkapatrāṇi yantre bhasmābhidhe kṣipet // Rsk_4.8 //
children.translated_text: smearing thin <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) leaves [with the paste], place them in the apparatus called <s>bhasma</s> (ash-apparatus). // Rsk_4.8 //
Kindle fire for eight <s>yāmas</s> (24 hours); when self-cooled, remove [the product];

children.text: viṣoṣaṇaṃ caturthāṃśaṃ dattvā vallamitā guṭī // Rsk_4.9 //
children.translated_text: adding one-fourth part of <s>viṣoṣaṇa</s> (desiccant), make pills the size of a <s>vallī</s>-seed. // Rsk_4.9 //
Bound with the juices of <s>devadālī</s> (Luffa), this preparation is [called] <s>Caitanyabhairava</s>;
given with ginger juice, it destroys all <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined-type) fevers. // Rsk_4.10 //

children.text: bhūmau gataṃ visaṃjñaṃ ca śītārtaṃ tandritaṃ naram /
children.translated_text: A person fallen to the ground, unconscious, afflicted by cold, or drowsy —
it revives him instantly; in [cases of] burning, one should employ cooling treatments. // Rsk_4.11 //
The five biles (<s>pitta</s>) are: of boar, goat, fish, horse, and peacock.
Treated with these, <s>Caitanyabhairava</s> [preparation] should also be administered. // Rsk_4.12 //
Poison and mercury in one-sixteenth proportion, in a glass-coated saucer,

children.text: ruddhvā cullyāṃ mandavahnau pacedyāmadvayaṃ tataḥ // Rsk_4.13 //
children.translated_text: having sealed, cook on a stove with gentle fire for two <s>yāmas</s> (watches). // Rsk_4.13 //
When self-cooled, one should collect from the upper saucer,
protecting from air, place in a bottle; in <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined <s>doṣa</s> disorder) and snakebite, // Rsk_4.14 //
it should be given on the tip of a needle; the person awakens in a moment.

children.text: no cet tālupradeśe ca kṣurakṣuṇṇe pracārayet // Rsk_4.15 //
children.translated_text: If not, it should be applied to the palate region after scraping with a razor. // Rsk_4.15 //
Mercury, sulfur, <s>Nepāla</s> (aconite), mature <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum), ground with water —

children.text: dvau yāmau jvaranāśāya guñjaikā sitayā saha // Rsk_4.16 //
children.translated_text: one <s>guñjā</s> (Abrus seed) dose with sugar, for the destruction of fever, [applied for] two <s>yāmas</s>. // Rsk_4.16 //
<s>Pura</s> (guggulu), borax, seeds of black <s>dhūrta</s> (Datura), eight pills,
three <s>pālikā</s> measures to be given — destroyer of quartan fever. // Rsk_4.17 //
At the time of the onset of fever, having bathed the head with four pots of cold water,

children.text: śiro 'bhiṣiñcya dātavyaṃ pathye kṣīraṃ saśarkaram // Rsk_4.18 //
children.translated_text: milk with sugar should be given as diet. // Rsk_4.18 //
Neem seeds, realgar, <s>jātī</s> (jasmine), fumigant, <s>kṛṣṇā</s> (long pepper), in equal parts,
to be processed with <s>kāravellī</s> (bitter gourd) juice twenty-one times. // Rsk_4.19 //
On whichever side the collyrium is applied to the eye, it conquers the fever arising from that side;
this mercury preparation named <s>Ardhanārīnaṭeśvara</s> is wonder-working. // Rsk_4.20 //

children.text: hiṅgulaṃ maricaṃ gandhaṃ pippalī ṭaṅkaṇaṃ viṣam /
children.translated_text: <s>Hiṅgula</s> (cinnabar), pepper, sulfur, <s>pippalī</s> (long pepper), borax, poison,

children.text: kanakasya tu bījāni samāṃśaṃ vijayārasaiḥ // Rsk_4.21 //
children.translated_text: and seeds of <s>Kanaka</s> (Datura) in equal parts, with <s>Vijayā</s> (Cannabis) juice — // Rsk_4.21 //
should be ground for one <s>yāma</s> (watch); pills the size of a chickpea are made.
<s>Hemasundara</s> (Golden Beauty) destroys fever, diarrhea, and <s>grahaṇī</s> (chronic digestive disorder). // Rsk_4.22 //
Purified mercury, one <s>pala</s> (measure), ground repeatedly with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk;
two <s>palas</s> of purified sulfur, eight <s>palas</s> of <s>mahākambū</s> (great conch shell) — // Rsk_4.23 //
both should be processed with <s>vahni</s> (Plumbago) juice, ground and dried for three days;
combine with the previous mercury and add half that amount of borax. // Rsk_4.24 //
Grind everything firmly again with <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk for one <s>yāma</s>;

children.text: tacchuṣkaṃ cūrṇalipte'tha bhāṇḍe ruddhvā puṭe pacet // Rsk_4.25 //
children.translated_text: when dried, seal in a powder-coated vessel and cook in a <s>puṭa</s> (sealed heating). // Rsk_4.25 //
One should eat a dose of four <s>guñjās</s> (Abrus seeds) combined with pepper and ghee;

children.text: deyaṃ dadhyodanaṃ pathyaṃ vijayā saguḍā niśi // Rsk_4.26 //
children.translated_text: the diet should be rice with yogurt; <s>Vijayā</s> (Cannabis) with jaggery at night. // Rsk_4.26 //
For the destruction of <s>grahaṇī</s> (digestive) disorders, there is nothing equal to this on earth;
the mercury preparation <s>Arkalokeśvara</s> destroys all <s>grahaṇī</s> afflictions. // Rsk_4.27 //
One [part] <s>tāla</s> (orpiment) processed with <s>kaṭutraya</s> (three pungents) juice and four [parts] <s>śilā</s> (realgar),
ground for a day with <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda) juice and cooked in a sand-bath apparatus. // Rsk_4.28 //
After two <s>yāmas</s>, extract and [add] an equal amount of <s>kaṭutraya</s> (three pungents),
and <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex) root powder, combined with <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda) juice. // Rsk_4.29 //
One <s>guñjā</s> dose of this <s>Śilātāleśvara</s> conquers asthma and cough.
Mercury, gold-mica <s>bhasma</s> (calcined ash), realgar, sulfur, and orpiment — // Rsk_4.30 //
making portions in the ratio of three, one, one, one, and one sequentially,
fill cowrie shells with this along with goat's milk and borax. // Rsk_4.31 //

children.text: piṣṭvā tena mukhaṃ ruddhvā śarāve bhūpuṭe pacet /
children.translated_text: Having ground and sealed the mouth with it, cook in a saucer in an earth-<s>puṭa</s>;
extract when self-cooled and strain through cloth. // Rsk_4.32 //
This mercury preparation <s>Rājamṛgāṅka</s> (Royal Moon), in four <s>guñjā</s> dose, destroys consumption (<s>kṣaya</s>).

children.text: suvarṇaṃ bhasmasūtaṃ ca vallārdhaṃ madhunā lihet // Rsk_4.33 //
children.translated_text: Gold, <s>bhasma</s>-mercury, half a <s>valla</s> (measure), should be licked with honey. // Rsk_4.33 //
With proper diet and celibacy, <s>Mṛgāṅka</s> (Moon) also destroys consumption.
<s>Śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch), honey, <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), and heated iron filings — whoever // Rsk_4.34 //
licks this with a milk diet, this <s>rasa</s> (preparation) quickly brings about the complete destruction of consumption.
Copper, <s>śyāmā</s> (black variety), <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia), <s>dantī</s> (Baliospermum), <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia), and <s>Nepāla</s> (aconite), in order — // Rsk_4.35 //
taking in proportions of one, two, one, one, one, and two parts, drink with warm water;
this destroys the eight types of abdominal diseases, especially <s>jalodara</s> (ascites). // Rsk_4.36 //
It destroys bloating, tumors, and colic — a sun dispelling the darkness of abdominal diseases.

children.text: dugdhaṃ śaṅkhavarāṭaṃ ca tulyārkaṃ navanītayuk // Rsk_4.37 //
children.translated_text: Milk, conch shell, cowrie, equal [part of] <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), combined with butter — // Rsk_4.37 //
one should consume half a <s>ṭaṅka</s> (measure); <s>Śaṅkhabhāskara</s> (Conch-Sun) destroys all colic.

children.text: śuddhaṃ sūtaṃ tathā gandhaṃ kramādekadvibhāgakam // Rsk_4.38 //
children.translated_text: Purified mercury and sulfur in proportions of one and two respectively — // Rsk_4.38 //
process with equal <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) and fresh ginger juice twenty-one times;

children.text: golaṃ kṛtvāndhamūṣāyāṃ ruddhvā gajapuṭe pacet // Rsk_4.39 //
children.translated_text: making a bolus, seal in a blind crucible and cook in a <s>gajapuṭa</s> (elephant-grade sealed heating). // Rsk_4.39 //

children.text: ghṛtaṃ śuṇṭhyā ca guñjaikaṃ śītodaṃ sasitaṃ hyanu /
children.translated_text: One <s>guñjā</s> with ghee and dry ginger; cold water with sugar as afterdrink —

children.text: tridoṣaṃ nāśayecchīghraṃ kriyāṃ śītāṃ prayojayet // Rsk_4.40 //
children.translated_text: it quickly destroys the three <s>doṣas</s>; one should employ cooling therapy. // Rsk_4.40 //
It makes the obese thin and the thin stout, and kindles the digestive fire.
Blood vitiated by the three <s>doṣas</s>, arising from wounds, sinuses, or injuries, // Rsk_4.41 //
and that which arises from the liver and spleen, and blood that causes skin diseases —
this mercury preparation called <s>Raktāri</s> (Enemy of Blood) purifies vitiated blood. // Rsk_4.42 //
Mercury, silver, <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) [salt], and <s>bola</s> (myrrh), ground with <s>arka</s> milk for three days;

children.text: vallaikaṃ madhunā lehyaṃ sthaulyamāśu vyapohati // Rsk_4.43 //
children.translated_text: one <s>valla</s> (measure) should be licked with honey — it quickly removes obesity. // Rsk_4.43 //
Then drink two <s>palas</s> of honey-cold-water as afterdrink;

children.text: vaḍavāgnirase pathyaṃ dadhyādi śleṣmalaṃ tyajet // Rsk_4.44 //
children.translated_text: with <s>Vaḍavāgni Rasa</s> (Submarine-Fire Preparation), one should avoid phlegm-producing diet like yogurt and the like. // Rsk_4.44 //
Mercury, <s>arka</s> [salt], and sulfur should be ground for a day with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex) juice;

children.text: yāmaikaṃ vālukāyantre paktvā deyo dviguñjakaḥ // Rsk_4.45 //
children.translated_text: cook for one <s>yāma</s> in a sand-bath apparatus; the dose is two <s>guñjās</s>. // Rsk_4.45 //
Afterward, give a decoction of citron rind with sugar as drink;
the preparation <s>Trivikrama Rasa</s> eliminates <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s> (dysuria) and <s>aśmarī</s> (urinary stones). // Rsk_4.46 //
Having dehusked twenty <s>palas</s> of <s>vākucī</s> (Psoralea) seeds,
[keep] in cow's urine for twenty-one days; iron and two <s>palas</s> of <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia) — // Rsk_4.47 //
taking [them] from the cow's urine, dry in intense sunshine;
process twenty-one times in a decoction of <s>kākodumbarikā</s> (Ficus hispida) bark, one <s>droṇa</s> [measure]. // Rsk_4.48 //
Process the powder with equal parts of sulfur and mercury;

children.text: amlena kajjalīṃ kṛtvā sarvamekatra kārayet // Rsk_4.49 //
children.translated_text: making <s>kajjalī</s> (black sulfide of mercury) with acid, combine everything together. // Rsk_4.49 //
Also with <s>śigru</s> (Moringa) root juice and <s>nāgavallī</s> (betel) leaves,

children.text: bhāvanāṃ tridinaṃ dattvā karṣārdhāṃśāṃ guṭīṃ kuru // Rsk_4.50 //
children.translated_text: giving processing for three days, make pills of half a <s>karṣa</s> [weight]. // Rsk_4.50 //
One should eat one each morning for the alleviation of <s>śvetakuṣṭha</s> (leucoderma);
powder of <s>citraka</s> (Plumbago) root bark at night in cow's milk is best. // Rsk_4.51 //
Add to yogurt, churn, and then collect the excellent buttermilk;
in one <s>kuḍava</s> (measure) of that buttermilk, place eight <s>vallas</s> of sulfur in the middle. // Rsk_4.52 //
Having dropped in the pill, afterward drink two or three [measures];
massage should be done with butter, then one should stand in sunlight. // Rsk_4.53 //
In all types of <s>śvitra</s> (leucoderma), blisters arise as if burned by fire;

children.text: prathame saptake pāko jāyetātha dvitīyake // Rsk_4.54 //
children.translated_text: ripening occurs in the first week, and then in the second — // Rsk_4.54 //

children.text: rohaṇaṃ ca tṛtīye hi prāpnuvanti na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: healing is certainly achieved in the third [week], without doubt;
application of saffron mixed with lemon juice is beneficial. // Rsk_4.55 //
Or the pill [dissolved] in buttermilk is also beneficial for external application of the preparation;

children.text: śvitrāṇāṃ rohaṇaṃ ramyaṃ varṇadaṃ jāyate bhṛśam // Rsk_4.56 //
children.translated_text: beautiful healing of leucoderma occurs, greatly restoring color. // Rsk_4.56 //

children.text: trivelaṃ takrabhaktaṃ ca pūrve deyaṃ ca saptake /
children.translated_text: Three times [daily], buttermilk and food should be given in the first week;

children.text: makuṣṭhām api rūkṣāśca deyā jāte dvisaptake // Rsk_4.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>makuṣṭha</s> (moth beans) and dry foods should be given starting from the second week. // Rsk_4.57 //
In the third week, moth beans, <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), and ghee should be given;

children.text: ghṛtamalpaṃ pradātavyaṃ śvitrakuṣṭhī varo bhavet // Rsk_4.58 //
children.translated_text: a small amount of ghee should be administered — the leucoderma patient becomes excellent. // Rsk_4.58 //

children.text: campakābhaṃ varaṃ dehaṃ kāntiyuktaṃ ca nīrujam /
children.translated_text: A body brilliant as <s>campaka</s> (Michelia champaca), excellent, endowed with radiance and free from disease —
the person, endowed with beauty, properly attains [this] on the surface of the earth, // Rsk_4.59 //
by the power of <s>Rasarāja</s> (King of Mercury) — truly, truly, and not otherwise.
Purified mercury, calcined iron, <s>tāpya</s> (pyrite), sulfur, and orpiment, // Rsk_4.60 //
<s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia), <s>agnimantha</s> (Premna), <s>nirguṇḍī</s> (Vitex), <s>tryūṣaṇa</s> (three pungents), borax, and poison —
in equal parts, grind in a mortar for a day with <s>nirguṇḍī</s> juice. // Rsk_4.61 //
[Then grind] for one day with <s>muṇḍī</s> (Sphaeranthus) juice; make pills of one <s>guñjā</s> [weight];
one afflicted with <s>vāta</s> (wind) diseases should consume [this] <s>Svacchandabhairava Rasa</s>. // Rsk_4.62 //
A decoction called <s>Laghu Rāsnā</s> with <s>pura</s> (guggulu) as afterdrink.
Purified mercury should then be ground for three days with <s>vacā</s> (Acorus calamus) decoction. // Rsk_4.63 //
Likewise add sulfur ground with <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> (Convolvulus) juice;
make a bolus ground with cow's urine and seal in a crucible. // Rsk_4.64 //
Having coated seven times with soft cloth, fire in a <s>puṭa</s> [and collect] when self-cooled;
powder it — four <s>vallas</s> [dose] with equal mustard powder. // Rsk_4.65 //

children.text: jīrṇadhṛtānupānaṃ ca nasye snehaṃ tu sārṣapam // Rsk_4.65 //
children.translated_text: Aged ghee as afterdrink, and mustard oil for nasal administration;
massage should be done with it for twenty-one days. // Rsk_4.66 //
It destroys mania and epilepsy — [this] <s>Unmādagajakeśarī</s> (Lion among Elephants of Madness).

children.text: sūtaṃ gandham ayas tāmram ekadvyardhārdhakaṃ palam /
children.translated_text: Mercury, sulfur, iron, and copper — one, two, half, and half <s>pala</s> [respectively]; // Rsk_4.67 //
melt in an iron vessel and place on castor leaves.

children.text: cūrṇitaṃ vastrapūtaṃ ca lohapātre punaḥ pacet /
children.translated_text: Having powdered and strained through cloth, one should cook it again in an iron vessel.

children.text: jāmbīraṃ baijapūraṃ vā rasaṃ pātramitaṃ kṣipet // Rsk_4.68 //
children.translated_text: One should add the juice of <s>jāmbīra</s> (lemon) or <s>baijapūra</s> (citron) in the measure of the vessel. (Rsk 4.68)
Having powdered it, with decoctions of the five spices (<s>pañcakola</s>) and <s>āmlavetasa</s> (tamarind),
fifty <s>bhāvanās</s> (levigations) should indeed be given thereafter. (Rsk 4.69)
One should add roasted <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax) powder in equal measure to all,
half the amount of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> should be <s>viḍa</s> (salt), and equal to <s>viḍa</s> should be <s>marīca</s> (black pepper). (Rsk 4.70)
One should levigate it seven times with water of <s>caṇaka</s> (chickpea) alkali,
thus from the perfected mercury, one or two or four pills [should be taken]. (Rsk 4.71)

children.text: saindhavaṃ māṣamekaṃ tu jīrakaṃ ca dvimāṣakam /
children.translated_text: <s>Saindhava</s> (rock salt) one <s>māṣa</s>, and <s>jīraka</s> (cumin) two <s>māṣas</s>,
combined with buttermilk, the wise person should drink this as an adjuvant. (Rsk 4.72)
One should eat heavy meat-based food up to the throat,

children.text: kṣipraṃ tajjīryate bhuktaṃ punaḥ kāṅkṣati bhojanam // Rsk_4.73 //
children.translated_text: that eaten food is quickly digested and one desires food again. (Rsk 4.73)
By <s>Ghaṭa</s> (pot, i.e., <s>Kumbha</s>), <s>Śravana</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Kumbhayoni</s> (Agastya), <s>Caturmukha</s> (Brahmā),
<s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> — it was served to <s>Agni</s> (the fire god). (Rsk 4.74)
By the constant use of this, all of them became great eaters (<s>mahāśana</s>),
therefore it is employed by kings for the great enhancement of digestive fire. (Rsk 4.75)

children.text: kuryāddīpanam adbhutaṃ pacanaṃ duṣṭāmayocchedanaṃ tundasthaulyanibarhaṇaṃ garaharaḥ śūlārtimūlāpahaḥ /
children.translated_text: It produces wonderful stimulation of digestive fire, digestion, destruction of severe diseases, removal of abdominal obesity, neutralization of poison, removal of the root of colic pain,

children.text: gulmaplīhavināśano bahurujāṃ vidhvaṃsanaḥ sraṃsano vātagranthimahodarāpaharaṇaḥ kravyādanāmā rasaḥ // Rsk_4.76 //
children.translated_text: destruction of abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>) and splenic enlargement (<s>plīha</s>), annihilation of many pains, purgation, removal of <s>vāta</s>-knots and great abdominal distension — this mercury is named <s>Kravyāda</s> (the flesh-eater). (Rsk 4.76)
To King <s>Sihaṇa</s>, who was fond of abundant food,

children.text: dattavān bhairavānando bhūpo grāmāṣṭakaṃ dadau // Rsk_4.77 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhairavānanda</s> gave [this preparation], and the king bestowed eight villages [in return]. (Rsk 4.77)

children.text: sūtaṃ bhujaṃgamamṛtaṃ lavaṇaṃ haridrā vyoṣaṃ dhanaṃjayajaṭāvanibhūtadhātrī /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (mercury), <s>bhujaṃgamamṛta</s> (snake venom), <s>lavaṇa</s> (salt), <s>haridrā</s> (turmeric), <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents), <s>dhanaṃjaya</s> (white leadwort), <s>jaṭā</s> (spikenard), <s>vanibhūta</s> (?), <s>dhātrī</s> (emblic myrobalan) —

in quantities of eighteen, two, nine, three, and four [respectively], with <s>śobhāñjana</s> (drumstick), fresh <s>ārdraka</s> (ginger), <s>karīra</s> (caper), and <s>bījapūra</s> (citron); (Rsk 4.78)

children.text: nimbūphaṇīśvaralatā supalāśatoyairbhāvyaṃ viśoṣya kharale prapidhāya cūrṇam /
children.translated_text: <s>nimbū</s> (lime), <s>phaṇīśvaralatā</s> (betel leaf), and water of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) — [the mixture] should be levigated, dried, and ground in a mortar into powder,
strained through cloth, it destroys all groups of <s>vāta</s> diseases, weakness of digestive fire, loss of appetite, colic, and vomiting. (Rsk 4.79)

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ viṣaṃ śaṅkhaṃ kapardaṃ ṭaṅkaṇoṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (mercury), <s>gandha</s> (sulfur), <s>viṣa</s> (aconite), <s>śaṅkha</s> (conch shell), <s>kaparda</s> (cowrie), <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), and <s>uṣaṇa</s> (long pepper) —
measured in parts of one (moon), one (fire), one (fire), eight (elephants), three, two, and eight (vasus), respectively. (Rsk 4.80)
Ground with <s>jambīra</s> (lemon) juice, it becomes <s>Agnikumāraka</s> (the fire-child [preparation]).
In <s>vāta</s> disorders, weak digestive fire, indigestion, fever, phlegm, and cholera, (Rsk 4.81)
it should be given in the dose of one <s>guñjā</s> (abrus seed weight), for afflictions of feces, urine, and the head,

children.text: kāse śvāse kṣaye śūle sarvaroge tu yojayet // Rsk_4.82 //
children.translated_text: in cough, asthma, consumption, colic — it should be employed in all diseases. (Rsk 4.82)
<s>Nṛsāra</s> (sal ammoniac), <s>sphaṭikā</s> (alum), and <s>saura</s> (?) — these three should be powdered together,

children.text: tatkṣipenmṛnmaye kūpe śubhe hastamite dṛḍhe // Rsk_4.83 //
children.translated_text: and placed into an auspicious, hand-sized, sturdy earthen pot. (Rsk 4.83)
In a pot with a perforated bottom made of glass, that [mixture] should be placed,
then the joint should be wrapped seven times with cloth and clay. (Rsk 4.84)
In a <s>kharpara</s> (shallow pan) filled with sand, the medicinal pot [should be placed] horizontally,

children.text: ardhaṃ yantre nidhāyātra śrīguroḥ saṃpradāyataḥ // Rsk_4.85 //
children.translated_text: half [submerged] in the apparatus, according to the tradition of the revered <s>Guru</s>. (Rsk 4.85)

children.text: adhomukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ tu sthāpyaṃ culleḥ parāṅmukhe /
children.translated_text: A second [pot] should be placed mouth-downward, facing away from the hearth,
and fire should be lit below forcefully until the mercury flows. (Rsk 4.86)
Then one should collect the conch-liquid mercury in a glass vessel,
and afterwards one should take one <s>śāṇa</s> dose, avoiding contact with the teeth. (Rsk 4.87)
It destroys abdominal tumors (<s>gulma</s>), abdominal distension, liver disorders, splenic enlargement, abscess, knots, and colic,

children.text: balapuṣṭiprado hyeṣa bhuktaṃ jārayate kṣaṇāt // Rsk_4.88 //
children.translated_text: and it bestows strength and nourishment; it digests eaten food in an instant. (Rsk 4.88)
Behold, O people, the wondrous greatness of mercury,

children.text: kapardakāmbulohāni yasmin kṣipte galanti hi // Rsk_4.89 //
children.translated_text: in which cowries, glass, and metals — when thrown — are dissolved! (Rsk 4.89)

children.text: pāradaṃ tattṛtīyāṃśaṃ gandhaṃ dattvā tu mardayet /
children.translated_text: One should grind <s>pārada</s> (mercury) with one-third its amount of <s>gandha</s> (sulfur),
combined with one-tenth <s>navasāra</s> (sal ammoniac) and <s>unmatta</s> (datura) water. (Rsk 4.90)
Having ground all of that in a mortar, one should place it in a glass flask,
within a sand-bath apparatus according to the tradition taught by the <s>Guru</s>. (Rsk 4.91)
One should cook it for sixteen <s>yāmas</s> (periods of three hours) with mild, moderate, and fierce fire,

children.text: pakvaḥ suśītalo grāhyo haragaurīraso bhavet // Rsk_4.92 //
children.translated_text: when cooked and fully cooled, it should be taken — it becomes <s>Haragaurīrasa</s> (the Śiva-Gaurī preparation). (Rsk 4.92)
Having made <s>sūta</s> (mercury) and <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) in equal parts, ground with the milk of <s>sarpākṣī</s> (Ophiorrhiza mungos),
cooked as before — others know this as <s>Haragaurīrasa</s>. (Rsk 4.93)
Having added <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) twice the amount of <s>pārada</s> (mercury), with the juices of <s>kārpāsikā</s> (cotton plant),
cooked as before — this is known as <s>Kāmadevarasa</s> (the love-god preparation). (Rsk 4.94)

children.text: samāṃśaṃ kṣipyate svarṇaṃ rūpyaṃ tāmraṃ ca mardayet /
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, and copper in equal parts should be added and ground
with <s>musalī</s> (Curculigo orchioides), <s>ākhuparṇī</s> (mouse-ear plant), and <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) juices for three days, (Rsk 4.95)
with <s>mocā</s> (plantain), <s>ciñcā</s> (tamarind), and <s>ātmaguptā</s> (Mucuna pruriens) — then it becomes <s>Mṛtyuñjayarasa</s> (the death-conquering preparation).
The intake of these three [preparations] is recommended; their virtues are described in order:

children.text: ekamāsaṃ sitājyābhyāṃ sadā sevyo narottamaiḥ // Rsk_4.96 //
children.translated_text: for one month, with sugar and ghee, it should always be taken by the best of men. (Rsk 4.96)

children.text: evaṃ niṣevya sūtendraṃ bhuñjīta madhuraṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Having thus consumed the lord of mercury, one should always eat sweet foods —

children.text: śālyannaṃ gopayaḥ khaṇḍaṃ sitāṃ jāṅgalamāmiṣam // Rsk_4.97 //
children.translated_text: <s>śāli</s> rice, cow's milk, <s>khaṇḍa</s> (raw sugar), white sugar, and meat from arid regions, (Rsk 4.97)
preparations made from wheat, food made with <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), banana fruit,

children.text: panasaṃ cātha kharjūraṃ drākṣāṃ ca nālikerakam // Rsk_4.98 //
children.translated_text: jackfruit, dates, grapes, and coconut. (Rsk 4.98)
The wise person should consume everything that is said to be aphrodisiac;

children.text: valīṃ saṃvatsarāddhanti palitaṃ ca dvihāyanāt // Rsk_4.99 //
children.translated_text: wrinkles are destroyed within a year, and grey hair within two years. (Rsk 4.99)
By its use, the body becomes adamantine (<s>vajradeha</s>); with two measures of the liquid, [one lives] a hundred [years];
there is no depletion of semen; even the impotent becomes virile. (Rsk 4.100)
The <s>liṅga</s> (phallus) always remains erect; one attains inexhaustible [capacity] with women;
one becomes like the color of heated gold, adorned with beauty, intellect, and wisdom. (Rsk 4.101)
Having the speed of a horse, the eyes of a peacock, and the hearing of a boar,
one becomes like another <s>Kāmadeva</s> (god of love), crushing the pride of proud women. (Rsk 4.102)
It destroys diseases like <s>rājayakṣmā</s> (consumption), <s>meha</s> (urinary disorders), and chronic fevers,
it destroys <s>grahaṇī</s> (sprue), diarrhea, and excessive urination [treated with] cow's buttermilk. (Rsk 4.103)
This indeed destroys all diseases when taken with the appropriate medicine as adjuvant;
<s>Haragaurī</s>, <s>Kāmadeva</s>, and <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s> are the names of these [three] preparations. (Rsk 4.104)
What more need be said? These three destroy old age and death.
<s>Kajjalī</s> (black sulfide of mercury) from mercury and sulfur in equal parts, with <s>unmattabīja</s> (datura seeds),
ground with that oil, two pills should be taken with sugar and milk. (Rsk 4.105)
It destroys a multitude of <s>meha</s> (urinary) disorders, makes semen firm, and makes women flow [with desire];
this mercury bestows desire to men, crushing the pride of proud women. (Rsk 4.106)
<s>Hema</s> (gold), <s>bīja</s> (seed/zinc), <s>viṣa</s> (aconite), <s>vaṅga</s> (tin), and <s>sūtaka</s> (mercury); <s>haṃsapāda</s> (realgar) and <s>jāraṇa</s> (calcination agent) —
purified mercury should be sweated for three days on mild fire in buffalo-milk curd;

children.text: truṭite truṭite dadyāddadhi turye'hni coddharet // Rsk_4.107 //
children.translated_text: at every cracking point, curd should be added; on the fourth day, it should be extracted. (Rsk 4.107)
The wise person should then add gold in a ratio of one to sixty-four parts of water,
and grind with <s>nimbū</s> (lime) juice until unity is achieved. (Rsk 4.108)
Again, that mercury should be sweated with the juices of <s>vaṭa</s> (banyan) shoots, <s>śuṅga</s> (?), and <s>ahivallī</s> (snake-creeper),

children.text: kākamācyā ca jīvantyā rasaiḥ syādyāmayugmakāt // Rsk_4.109 //
children.translated_text: <s>kākamācī</s> (black nightshade) and <s>jīvantī</s> (Leptadenia reticulata), for a pair of <s>yāmas</s> (six hours). (Rsk 4.109)
One day [it should be kept] in a pot of cold water, one day in buffalo-milk curd;
thus from the perfected mercury, a pill [should be taken] daily, observing <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy). (Rsk 4.110)
The husband should take it for one month, being fond of rice with sugar and milk;
the wife [should take it] separately in order, with the juices of <s>triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>nimbaka</s> (neem), and <s>kārpāsī</s> (cotton plant). (Rsk 4.111)
Having drunk [this] for seven days in number, at the time of the menstrual union,

children.text: rasaṃ vallaṃ tryahaṃ caikaṃ kārpāsyambusitāyutam // Rsk_4.112 //
children.translated_text: the mercury pill for three days and one day with <s>kārpāsī</s> water and sugar. (Rsk 4.112)
<s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s> (borax), <s>sphaṭikā</s> (alum), and <s>sūta</s> (mercury), combined with the juice of ripe tamarind,

children.text: tridinaṃ madhunā yonerlepaṃ śuddhikaraṃ param // Rsk_4.113 //
children.translated_text: applied as a paste to the vagina for three days with honey — this is the supreme purifier. (Rsk 4.113)
Mercury of three <s>māṣas</s>, placed in buffalo-milk curd during the day,
should be consumed at night at the time of sexual union, combined with curd. (Rsk 4.114)

children.text: saṃbhogānte tathā stheyaṃ yāmārdhaṃ saṃpuṭena ca /
children.translated_text: After intercourse, one should remain for half a <s>yāma</s> (one and a half hours) in the coupled position;
[this] mercury produces an excellent son endowed with all auspicious marks. (Rsk 4.115)
When fever and the like arise [during pregnancy], grape juice, sugar, and similar [remedies] should be given;

children.text: kāryaḥ śītopacāraśca yuvatyā bhiṣajā sadā // Rsk_4.116 //
children.translated_text: cooling treatments should always be administered by the physician to the young woman. (Rsk 4.116)
It produces increase of lifespan, strength, radiance, and enhancement of lost virility;
it destroys diseases and bestows sons — this was fashioned by <s>Rudra</s>. (Rsk 4.117)
Mercury, <s>nāgāñjana</s> (lead collyrium), and <s>candra</s> (camphor), in parts of one, one, and one-and-a-half respectively,
finely powdered — by application as collyrium to the eyes, it produces divine vision. (Rsk 4.118)

children.text: sūtaṃ gandhaṃ samaṃ śuddhaṃ saptadhā bhāvayet kramāt /
children.translated_text: <s>Sūta</s> (mercury) and <s>gandha</s> (sulfur) in equal parts, purified, should be levigated seven times in order

with the milks of <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia neriifolia) and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), and with the juices of the two varieties of <s>śrīkhaṇḍa</s> (sandalwood) and <s>pathyā</s> (Terminalia chebula). (Rsk 4.119)
An equal amount of Nepali powder should be added and ground together;
two pills should be given with warm water, in eight times [their weight] of <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery). (Rsk 4.120)

children.text: malāḥ pūrvaṃ jalaṃ paścāttataścāmaḥ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ /
children.translated_text: First the impurities [are expelled], then watery [stools], then gradually soft [stools];

children.text: udarācca vināntrāṇi sarvaṃ niryāti kilbiṣam // Rsk_4.121 //
children.translated_text: and from the abdomen, through the intestines, all impurity is expelled. // Rsk_4.121 //

children.text: jāte vireke saṃśuddhe pathyaṃ dadhyodanaṃ hitam /
children.translated_text: When purgation has occurred and [the patient] is cleansed, rice with yogurt is the recommended wholesome diet;
this preparation called <s>Sāraṇasundara</s> (Beautiful Purgative) conquers fevers and other diseases. // Rsk_4.122 //
Lead-tin alloy, <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), and licorice in the ratio of one, one-and-a-half, two, and five parts,

children.text: ṭaṅkaiko'mbuyuto datto raso'yaṃ vāmakaḥ smṛtaḥ // Rsk_4.123 //
children.translated_text: one part borax, given with water — this preparation is known as an emetic. // Rsk_4.123 //

children.text: rasaṃ gandhaṃ samaṃ vyoṣaṃ mardyamunmattakair dinam /
children.translated_text: Mercury and sulfur in equal parts, with <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents), ground for a day with <s>unmattaka</s> (Datura) [juice] —

children.text: unmattākhyo raso nāma nasyaṃ syātsannipātajit // Rsk_4.124 //
children.translated_text: the preparation called <s>Unmatta</s> (Maddening) is used as a nasal medication and conquers <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined-type) fever. // Rsk_4.124 //

children.text: tāmrapatraṃ gandhaliptaṃ vahnau taptaṃ tu tāḍitam /
children.translated_text: A copper plate smeared with sulfur, heated in fire and hammered —
that powder, mixed with buttermilk, half a <s>vallī</s>-weight, powerfully induces emesis. // Rsk_4.125 //
Crystal alum, copper sulfate, Nepal [aconite], pepper, neem seeds,
<s>putrajīvaka</s> (Putranjiva roxburghii) kernel — [ground] with lemon [juice] in a <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) leaf vessel; // Rsk_4.126 //
seven levigations should be given; a pill of one <s>guñjā</s>-weight used as collyrium
destroys <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined fever), epilepsy, and snake venom. // Rsk_4.127 //
<s>Ākallaka</s>, black poison (<s>viṣa</s>), and ash of <s>hemadru</s> (golden tree) fruit —
used as a dusting powder, it removes perspiration, in proportions of one, two, three, and eight parts. // Rsk_4.128 //
RSK, 5
Poison (<s>viṣa</s>, i.e. aconite), <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), turmeric, <s>abda</s> (Cyperus), neem leaves, and <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia) —

children.text: guṭī chāgāmbunā baddhā syājjayā yogavāhikā // Rsk_5.1 //
children.translated_text: a pill bound with goat's urine; this is <s>Jayā</s> (Victorious), a synergistic carrier (<s>yogavāhikā</s>). // Rsk_5.1 //
Mercury, <s>arka</s> (Calotropis), poison, sulfur, <s>viḍaṅga</s>, Ganges [water], fire [salt], <s>abda</s> (Cyperus), and saffron,

children.text: reṇukā granthikaṃ bolaṃ sarveṣāṃ dviguṇaṃ guḍam // Rsk_5.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>reṇukā</s>, <s>granthika</s> (dried ginger), myrrh — and jaggery double the amount of all [others]; // Rsk_5.2 //
one should eat a pill the size of a jujube fruit, indeed in the early morning,

children.text: kāse śvāse kṣaye gulme pramehe viṣamajvare // Rsk_5.3 //
children.translated_text: for cough, asthma, consumption, abdominal tumors, urinary diseases, and intermittent fever; // Rsk_5.3 //
for grief, anemia, leprosy, <s>grahaṇī</s> (sprue), hemorrhoids, and fistula —
this is the <s>Vijayā</s> (Victorious) pill, taught by <s>Rudra</s>, superior in its qualities. // Rsk_5.4 //
