children.text: aṅkolāgnī ca gandhoṣaṇarasaviṣakaṃ pittabhājaṃ kramāttatsāmudraṃ cārkadugdhaistribhiratha puṭitaṃ nimbutoyairvimardya /
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅkola</s>, fire-salt, sulfur, dry ginger, mercury, poison, and <s>pitta</s>-bile [corrective] — in sequence; then sea salt and <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) milk — processed three times in a fire-pit, then ground with lemon juice;

children.text: kṛtvā guñjāsamānām iṣuśararasadigvahnibāṇeṣudigbhir dadyācchleṣmānilārśo jvaraṃ jaṭharaṃ kaphetāṃ vaṭīṃ śaṅkarākhyām // Rsk_5.5 //
children.translated_text: making [pills] equal to a <s>guñjā</s>-weight, one should administer them in doses of five-five-four-ten-three-two for phlegm-wind-hemorrhoids-fever-abdominal [diseases] and phlegm — this pill is called <s>Śaṅkara</s> (auspicious). // Rsk_5.5 //

children.text: ciñcākṣārapalaṃ paṭuvrajapalaṃ nimbūrasaiḥ kalkitaṃ tasmiñchaṅkhapalaṃ prataptamasakṛnnirvāpya śīrṇāvadhim /
children.translated_text: One <s>pala</s> of tamarind alkali and one <s>pala</s> of <s>paṭu</s> (rock salt) made into a paste with lemon juice; in that, one <s>pala</s> of conch-shell heated and quenched repeatedly until it crumbles;

children.text: hiṅguvyoṣapalaṃ rasāmṛtabalīnnikṣipya niṣkāṃśakān baddhā śaṅkhavaṭī kṣayagrahaṇikāgulmāṃśca śūlaṃ jayet // Rsk_5.6 //
children.translated_text: adding one <s>pala</s> of <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida) and <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), and one <s>niṣka</s>-weight each of mercury, mica, and iron calx — the pill bound [thus] is <s>Śaṅkhavaṭī</s>, which conquers consumption, <s>grahaṇī</s> (sprue), abdominal tumors, and colic. // Rsk_5.6 //

children.text: rasaṃ kṛṣṇābhayā tvakṣaṃ vāsā bhārgī kramottaram /
children.translated_text: Mercury, black <s>abhayā</s> (myrobalan), cinnamon bark, <s>vāsā</s> (Adhatoda), <s>bhārgī</s> (Clerodendrum) — each increasing in sequence;
an equal amount of <s>khadira</s> (catechu) essence, levigated with <s>babbūla</s> (acacia) decoction; // Rsk_5.7 //
twenty-one times [levigated]; a pill the size of an <s>akṣa</s> (Terminalia bellirica) [taken] with honey

children.text: kāsaṃ śvāsaṃ kṣayaṃ hikkāṃ hantyeṣā kāsakartarī // Rsk_5.8 //
children.translated_text: destroys cough, asthma, consumption, and hiccup — this is <s>Kāsakartarī</s> (Cough-Cutter). // Rsk_5.8 //

children.text: vyoṣagranthi vacāgni hiṃgu jaraṇadvandvaṃ viṣaṃ nimbukaṃ drāvair ārdrakair aservimṛṣitaṃ tulyau marīcopamā /
children.translated_text: <s>Vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), <s>granthi</s> (dried ginger), <s>vacā</s> (Acorus), fire-salt, <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), the two digestives, poison, and lemon — ground with fresh ginger juice, equal in size to a pepper [grain];

children.text: vartiḥ sā vinihanti śūlamakhilaṃ sarvāṅgajaṃ mārutam vahniṃ cāśu karoti vāḍavasamaṃ sūryaprabhāvābhidhā // Rsk_5.9 //
children.translated_text: this wick destroys all colic, all <s>vāta</s> (wind) disorders of the entire body, and quickly makes the digestive fire equal to the submarine fire — it is called <s>Sūryaprabhāvā</s> (Power of the Sun). // Rsk_5.9 //

children.text: elā sakarpūrasitā sadhātrī jātīphalaṃ śālmaligokṣurau ca /
children.translated_text: Cardamom with camphor and sugar, <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry), nutmeg, <s>śālmali</s> (silk-cotton tree), and <s>gokṣura</s> (Tribulus);
calx of mercury, tin, and iron — all in equal amounts, should be levigated; // Rsk_5.10 //

children.text: guḍūcikā śālmalikā kaṣāyair niṣkārdhamānā madhunā tataśca /
children.translated_text: with decoctions of <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora) and <s>śālmali</s> (silk-cotton tree); half a <s>niṣka</s>-weight, then with honey

children.text: baddhā guṭī candrakaleti saṃjñā meheṣu sarveṣu niyojanīyā // Rsk_5.11 //
children.translated_text: a pill is bound, named <s>Candrakalā</s> (Moonbeam) — it should be employed in all types of urinary disease (<s>meha</s>). // Rsk_5.11 //
Cinnabar, the four spices (<s>caturjāta</s>), clove, <s>auṣadha</s> (dried ginger), sandalwood,
nutmeg, saffron, black pepper, <s>ākalla</s> (aconite), and <s>mahiphena</s> (cuttle-bone); // Rsk_5.12 //
all equal to musk and camphor; in the same amount, <s>vijayā</s> (cannabis) and sugar —

children.text: kṣaudraiḥ kolamitā kāryā guṭī bhogapurandarī // Rsk_5.13 //
children.translated_text: pills the size of a jujube fruit should be made with honey: [this is] <s>Bhogapurandarī</s> (Queen of Pleasure). // Rsk_5.13 //
This causes firmness of semen; it increases strength and flesh;
a man goes like a sparrow a hundred times, with firm senses. // Rsk_5.14 //
Tin, green vitriol (<s>kāsīsa</s>), and black pepper — one <s>guñjā</s>-weight with fresh ginger water;
this pill called <s>Nāgārjunā</s> destroys <s>kapha</s> (phlegm) and <s>vāta</s> (wind) diseases. // Rsk_5.15 //
<s>Triphalā</s> (three fruits), <s>viḍaṅga</s> (Embelia), <s>soma</s> (Ephedra), <s>abhallātaka</s> (marking-nut), fire-salt, and <s>viśva</s> (dried ginger) —
eight parts of white <s>vacā</s> (Acorus) and one part of poison with six [parts];
all this ground with cow's urine, pills the size of chickpeas,
dried in shade — should be given by the wise in doses of three, two, one, or four in sequence. // Rsk_5.16 //
For one afflicted by snake [bite], cholera, or [other] diseases, struck by indigestion, or with all three <s>doṣas</s> vitiated —

children.text: sadyo jīvati puruṣo mṛto'pi guṭikāprabhāveṇa // Rsk_5.17 //
children.translated_text: a person revives instantly, even if dead, by the power of this pill. // Rsk_5.17 //

children.text: mūlena patreṇa phalena vāpi vyoṣānvitā yā kitavodbhavena /
children.translated_text: Whether with root, leaf, or fruit of <s>kitava</s> (Strychnos) combined with <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents),

children.text: baddhā guṭī sā sahasaiva hanti sonmādadoṣatrayaduṣṭavātān // Rsk_5.18 //
children.translated_text: a pill bound [thus] instantly destroys deranged <s>vāta</s> vitiated by all three <s>doṣas</s>, accompanied by madness. // Rsk_5.18 //
<s>Kaṭphala</s> (Myrica), water, <s>gila</s> (a resin), black pepper, cinnabar, myrrh, and borax —

children.text: guḍena guṭikā śāṇamitā sā navame'hni // Rsk_5.19 //
children.translated_text: a pill of one <s>śāṇa</s>-weight made with jaggery, [given] on the ninth day; // Rsk_5.19 //
should be given with warm water — it instantly removes rabid dog poison;

children.text: garabhṛṅgoṣaṇaṃ cūrṇaṃ sājyaṃ vā tadviṣāpaham // Rsk_5.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>gara</s>-poison [is removed by] <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta) and dry ginger powder with ghee, or it removes that poison. // Rsk_5.20 //
With mercury-king, copper, sulfur, <s>suratikta</s> (Gentian), yellow <s>bhṛṅga</s> (Eclipta), and pepper,
pills the size of chickpeas should be made, enhanced with the juice of both types of <s>brāhmī</s>; // Rsk_5.21 //
one should be given first to one afflicted by the three <s>doṣas</s>, even if unconscious;

children.text: anyā muhūrtaparataḥ praharād anyāparā naiva // Rsk_5.22 //
children.translated_text: another after one <s>muhūrta</s> (48 minutes), another after one <s>prahara</s> (3 hours), and no more after that. // Rsk_5.22 //
A person revives even if dead, afflicted by all three <s>doṣas</s>, with drowsiness and lethargy;
this pill spoken by the illustrious <s>Nāgārjuna</s> is renowned as <s>Mṛtasaṃjīvanī</s> (Reviver of the Dead). // Rsk_5.23 //
<s>Elavāluka</s> (cardamom), <s>abhayā</s> (myrobalan), myrrh, <s>indrā</s> (Wrightia), combined with <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) —
a pill [made] with <s>snuhī</s> (Euphorbia) milk; it reduces swelling and destroys fever. // Rsk_5.24 //

children.text: varā vyoṣaṃ varaṃ tutthaṃ yaṣṭī vellārkavārijam /
children.translated_text: <s>Varā</s> (Terminalia chebula), <s>vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), the best copper sulfate, licorice, cardamom, <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) water,

children.text: rodhraṃ rasāñjanaṃ cūrṇaṃ vartiḥ kāryā nabho'mbunā // Rsk_5.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>rodhra</s> (Symplocos), <s>rasāñjana</s> (extract of Berberis) — make into a powder and wick with rain water. // Rsk_5.25 //
It instantly [cures] eye inflammation with breast milk; cataract with <s>rodhra</s> water;

children.text: kiṃśukasya rasāddhanti billaṃ puṣpaṃ ca raktatām // Rsk_5.26 //
children.translated_text: with the juice of <s>kiṃśuka</s> (Butea) it destroys opacity; and [its] flower [cures] redness. // Rsk_5.26 //
Cataract-film (<s>paṭala</s>) [is treated] with goat's urine; for stiffness, with <s>pāṭali</s> (Stereospermum) extract —
written by <s>Nāgārjuna</s>, this removes all eye diseases. // Rsk_5.27 //

children.text: vyoṣaṃ varā varaṃ hiṅgu tiktogrā naktamālakaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vyoṣa</s> (three pungents), <s>varā</s> (Terminalia chebula), the best [copper sulfate], <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), <s>tikta</s> (Gentian), <s>ugrā</s> (Acorus), <s>naktamālaka</s> (Pongamia),

children.text: gaurī kaṭu tvajāmūtraiś chāyāśuṣkā guṭīkṛtā // Rsk_5.28 //
children.translated_text: <s>gaurī</s> (turmeric), pungent [substances] — made into pills with goat's urine, dried in shade. // Rsk_5.28 //
It destroys epilepsy, memory loss, madness, and headache;

children.text: naktāndhyaṃ timiraṃ hanti doṣaṃ bhūtādikaṃ bhramam // Rsk_5.29 //
children.translated_text: night-blindness, cataract, disorders caused by evil spirits, and vertigo. // Rsk_5.29 //
Fevers called first-day, second-day, third-day, and fourth-day [types] through anointing,
and <s>saṃnipāta</s> (combined) [fever] with unconsciousness — it destroys them, restoring full consciousness. // Rsk_5.30 //
<s>Vajrī</s> (Euphorbia) milk mixed with rock salt, cooked on fire,
drunk in a dose of two <s>vallī</s>-weights with warm water — through purgation, it destroys fever. // Rsk_5.31 //
Salt levigated once with <s>bhānu</s> (Calotropis) milk in sunlight —

children.text: gavyena payasā pītaṃ karṣārdhaṃ vāntikārakam // Rsk_5.32 //
children.translated_text: drunk with cow's milk, half a <s>karṣa</s>-weight, it induces emesis. // Rsk_5.32 //

children.text: sūtendraṃ balitālakaṃ ca kunaṭī khalve samāṃśaṃ dinaṃ sauvīreṇa vimardya tena vasanaṃ vartīkṛtaṃ lepayet /
children.translated_text: Mercury-king, orpiment, and <s>kunaṭī</s> (Hellebore) — in equal parts, ground in a mortar for one day with <s>sauvīra</s> (vinegar), then smear a cloth made into a wick with that;

children.text: tailena pravilepitaṃ ca bahuśo vahniṃ tato dīpayet tasmādyadgalitaṃ tu tailamasitaṃ tenāṅgalepaḥ kṛtaḥ // Rsk_5.33 //
children.translated_text: smear it repeatedly with oil, then kindle a fire from it; the black oil that drips from it — with that, apply a body liniment. // Rsk_5.33 //
It conquers tremors of the calves, arms, hands, feet, and head completely; it [cures] leprosy, severe fistula, collections of wounds, diseases, and <s>mahāgṛdhrasī</s> (severe sciatica);
and other groups of diseases born of <s>vāta</s> (wind), and intractable sinus ulcers —

children.text: vikhyātaṃ bhuvanatraye gadaharaṃ vātāritailaṃ mahat // Rsk_5.34 //
children.translated_text: renowned in the three worlds as disease-destroying, this is the great <s>Vātāri Taila</s> (Wind-Enemy Oil). // Rsk_5.34 //
<s>Rāmaṭha</s> (asafoetida), neem leaves, and foam of oceanic origin [sea-foam],

children.text: etāni samabhāgāni tadvaddeyaṃ sitaṃ viṣam // Rsk_5.35 //
children.translated_text: these in equal parts, and likewise an equal amount of white poison (<s>viṣa</s>, i.e. aconite); // Rsk_5.35 //
cook pungent oil combined with cow's urine,
and fill the ears of men, elephants, and horses with it. // Rsk_5.36 //
It quickly destroys ear disease; through application, it [cures] diseases of the head —

children.text: nāmnā karṇāmṛtaṃ tailaṃ brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ svayam // Rsk_5.37 //
children.translated_text: this oil named <s>Karṇāmṛta</s> (Ear-Nectar) was created by <s>Brahmā</s> himself. // Rsk_5.37 //

children.text: kastūrīnduśca bāhlīkaṃ nakhaṃ māṃsī ca sarjakam /
children.translated_text: Musk, camphor, <s>bāhlīka</s> (saffron), <s>nakha</s> (nail-shaped shell), <s>māṃsī</s> (spikenard), and <s>sarjaka</s> (resin),

children.text: mustāguru sitā sarvaṃ kramavṛddhaṃ samaṃ puram // Rsk_5.38 //
children.translated_text: <s>mustā</s> (Cyperus), <s>aguru</s> (aloeswood), and sugar — all in progressively increasing [amounts], equal [total], with <s>pura</s> (camphor). // Rsk_5.38 //
Add oil little by little, then pound for one day;

children.text: vartiṃ nirvāpayet dīptāṃ divyaṃ dhūmaṃ vimuñcati // Rsk_5.39 //
children.translated_text: extinguish the blazing wick — it releases a divine fragrance. // Rsk_5.39 //
Beloved by all gods, it grants success in all <s>mantras</s>;
whether in bathing, on garments, or in the pleasure chamber — this incense is favored by kings.
In the year measured by earth-fire-lunar day [i.e. Śaka era], <s>Cāmuṇḍa</s>, in the city of <s>Yoginīpura</s> (Delhi),
composed this <s>Rasasaṃketakalikā</s>, which grants the fulfillment of desires. // Rsk_5.40 //
